item.title: NASA hopes the commercial space industry can help save Hubble
item.description: Gravity is a cruel mistress, slowly dragging the famed telescope ever closer to its ultimate demise with every day. Hubble is in no immediate danger of burning up in the Earth's atmosphere, but its time will run out in the early to mid 2030s unless its orbit is boosted. So NASA is taking proposals from the private sector to see if anyone can save it. In a post on NASA's site , Administrator Jared Isaacman said: "Hubble still has important science ahead of it, and we should be looking at every reasonable opportunity to keep it delivering for as long as possible … If there are innovative and cost-effective ways to extend the life of an asset … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Lions’ Brian Branch, DJ Wonnum both suffer concussions in heated Vikings showdown
item.description: Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Lions’ Brian Branch, DJ Wonnum both suffer concussions in heated Vikings showdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday, the Detroit Lions hit the field at home for a key NFC North showdown against the Minnesota Vikings . The Lions were looking to build off their momentum from last week’s win over the Green Bay Packers and hand the Vikings their first loss of the season in the process. Unfortunately, the Lions didn’t make it through this game unscathed from an injury perspective , as two members of their defense suffered the same injury in this one. “#Lions Injury Update: EDGE DJ Wonnum (Concussion) has been downgraded to Out. DB Brian Branch (Concussion) has been downgraded to Out,” reported the team on its official account on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Earlier in the game, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had been evaluated for a concussion, but thankfully was cleared to return to the game, having suffered his own injury on a play in which a touchdown was wiped from the board after replay review. Meanwhile, Branch only recently returned to the field after missing the first several games of this season, having torn his Achilles down the stretch of last season. If Wonnum and Branch are forced to miss extended time with their concussions, it would certainly be a tough break for a Lions defense that was just starting to round into form this season. In any case, at the conclusion of the Vikings game, the Lions will hit the field next week on the road vs the lowly Miami Dolphins. Kickoff for that game is set for 1:00 pm ET. Related: Ranking top 3 Vikings most likely to be dealt at 2026 NFL trade deadline Related: Vikings WR Justin Jefferson’s stats may be down, but he just reminded everybody how ridiculous he really is

item.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos sail into semi finals, to meet Brazil
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos booked their place in the semi-finals of this year’s FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup finals after securing a 1-0 victory over Venezuela on Sunday night, with Azeezatt Oduntan scoring a late penalty in the 89th minute. The quarter-final contest had been closely fought, with Nigeria creating several opportunities but finding Venezuela goalkeeper Valeria Rebanales a huge stumbling block. The Flamingos enjoyed much of the attacking play in the first half, but Rebanales produced a couple of saves to keep the scores level. Midfielder Favour Nkwocha was also cautioned as Nigeria continued to press for an opening goal. Head Coach Hakeem Busari made his first change of the evening, introducing Precious Oscar for Oluwakemi Adegbuyi as Nigeria looked to find a way through. The deadlock remained unbroken until the 88th minute, when the referee initially awarded Nigeria a penalty before being invited to the VAR monitor to review the decision. Following the review, the penalty was upheld, and Oduntan stepped forward to convert from the spot with a minute left on the clock, giving Nigeria the breakthrough. Top scorer Oluebube Umejiaku had won the penalty for the Flamingos, setting up Oduntan to deliver the decisive moment of the contest. The victory sends Nigeria into the semi-finals, where they will face Brazil, who secured a 2-1 win over China in their quarter-final encounter. The post FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos sail into semi finals, to meet Brazil appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: From Fleetwood embarrassment to 'magical' Anfield win 14 years in making
item.description: "Today has to be the day." That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal . Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory. The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win. Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool. "Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game. "I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. "Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it. "Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do." Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool. That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break. Although the second half was a bit calmer, they still defended resolutely and did not allow Liverpool a shot on target. The Gunners, who have kept six clean sheets this season, are now three points clear at the top of the table after nine games. I'll tell my players to dive in future - Iraola Arsenal have kept six clean sheets in the Premier League this season [Getty Images] 'The togetherness we have is undefeated' Arsenal's 24 points is the most by any team after nine games of a season since the Gunners themselves in 2022-23. And only in the 2004-05 and 2007-08 seasons have Arsenal had more at this stage of a Premier League season. "It means a lot to our football club," match winner Havertz said after the win. "It's been 13 games [in the Premier League without a win here], its a crazy stat and it's what the fans deserve. We are happy we gave them that." The win was also the first time that Arsenal had kept a clean sheet at Anfield in the Premier League since that victory in 2012. "That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do, this is what this stadium does to you," Declan Rice - who assisted Havertz's goal - added. "That is the Anfield way, that is what this Liverpool team can do, this is what this stadium does to you," Declan Rice - who assisted Havertz's goal - added. "It just creates waves and waves of attack. "We've not won here in 14 years. It was relentless attacks but in the end that way we stuck together, that togetherness we have is undefeated. It's nothing like I've ever seen before." Rice has been one of Arsenal's standout players this season and has five assists in the league already Arsenal set for title defence Arsenal are now two points better off after nine games of this campaoign than last season, when they won the title. The Gunners attack is not yet flowing and they have scored just 14 league goals in nine games Arteta has been restricted with his options in the forward line with Bukayo Saka out injured, 16-year-old Max Dowman suspended after his red card at Fleetwood, Christos Tzolis just back from a hamstring injury, and Viktor Gyokeres and Havertz both struggling for form. But the Arsenal defence is an elite unit. The back four only conceded 27 goals last season and, on this performance, they could once again be the difference for the Gunners. "I'm extremely proud; this is something you want to accomplish." Arteta said after being asked what the win against Liverpool means to him. "That's the challenge and mission you want to accomplish. I love it when it's something we have not done for many years. "It was the same with Chelsea away and Manchester United away. To be able to beat all those, that's the purpose and motivation and why we do what we do." Manchester City are second in the table but are waiting to find out what happens, pending their appeal, following their charge for breaching the Premier League financial rules . And with the rest of the big-name sides in the league in a period of transition, Arsenal could find themselves with a healthy lead at the top of the table of the table if things carry on as they are. item.title: Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel artist to hit one billion YouTube views
item.description: Nigerian gospel singer and pastor Nathaniel Bassey has surpassed one billion views on YouTube, becoming the first African gospel artist to achieve the milestone. Bassey’s official YouTube channel, Nathaniel Bassey Main, has amassed more than 1.014 billion views and 5.24 million subscribers since its creation in 2011, according to figures displayed on the platform at the time of filing this report. The achievement coincides with the October 2026 edition of the Hallelujah Challenge, the online prayer and worship programme founded by the gospel minister in 2017. The monthly initiative features midnight sessions of praise, worship and prayers, attracting participants from different parts of the world. Initially launched as an online worship gathering, the Hallelujah Challenge has grown into an international Christian movement, with thousands of people participating in its live sessions and millions more watching recorded editions. Bassey is known for popular gospel songs such as Imela , Onise Iyanu , Olowogbogboro and You Are God , which have contributed to his popularity among gospel music audiences in Nigeria and beyond. The one-billion-view milestone has generated excitement among his followers, with some suggesting that the minister could explore opportunities to monetise the growing audience of his online worship sessions. However, Bassey has maintained that the Hallelujah Challenge is primarily focused on worship and spiritual devotion rather than revenue generation. Vanguard News The post Nathaniel Bassey becomes first African gospel artist to hit one billion YouTube views appeared first on Vanguard News .

However, Bassey has maintained that the Hallelujah Challenge is primarily focused on worship and spiritual devotion rather than revenue generation. item.title: Shelton adds former Alcaraz coach Ferrero to team
item.description: Ben Shelton says he's adding former world number one Juan Carlos Ferrero to his coaching team (Hector RETAMAL) Ben Shelton, who reached his first Grand Slam final at the US Open in September, is adding former Carlos Alcaraz mentor Juan Carlos Ferrero to his team, both parties said Sunday. "Huge addition to my team for this upcoming season," Shelton said in an Instagram story featuring a photo of himself and Spain's Ferrero. "Excited to get started ... Let's get it." Shelton, 24, is at a career-high fourth in the world with a career-best four titles in 2026. The American left-hander reached his first major final in New York, beating Alcaraz in a five-set quarter-final but eventually falling to Alexander Zverev in the title match. Shelton has largely been coached by his father, Bryan Shelton, winner of two singles titles in his own ATP playing career. Spain's Ferrero, who guided Alcaraz to his first six Grand Slam titles before their partnership ended last December, said he was looking forward to working with both the elder and younger Sheltons. "Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character," Ferrero said in a statement. "I'm very happy to join Bryan and the team in this exciting new chapter. I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together to help Ben achieve his ambitions on the biggest stages." Ben Shelton also emphasized that Ferrero, a former world number one and winner of the 2003 Roland Garros title, would be an addition to the current team, not a replacement. "Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said in a statement. "His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team. "My dad has been such an important part of my journey, and I'm excited about what we can all achieve together as we look to the future." bb/js

item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) hands the ball to running back Bucky Irving (7) against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Would a second consecutive game of relentless running by the Buccaneers’ offense be enough for the Buccaneers to climb out of their early season hole and to the top of the NFC South? First Quarter: It was Todd Bowles’ defense up first on Sunday. Battling on a water-logged field, Tampa’s strongest unit took the field and bent a bit, however, there was no break. The Falcons pushed into Tampa territory before ultimately needing to settle for a long field goal attempt. Weather conditions not favoring Nick Folk, the kick was missed and missed badly. Converting turnovers into points or this case missed field goals into points gave Tampa the first lead of the day. 3-0, Buccaneers. The response from the Falcons was quite mild, an interception by Alex Anzalone. Penix looking for Drake London on a slant, found Anzalone for his second interception of the season. Turnovers into points would fail Tampa on their next drive— Bucky Ivring, breaking into space on a broken play, was met by Jessie Bates at the goal line for a 2023 Antoine Winfield Jr.-esque forced fumble stripping the ball out at the goal line which rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Rest assured, Tampa’s defense understood the assignment. Back on the field, following an Alex Anzalone pick that didn’t result into points, fans watched Michael Penix drop back and throw another Alex Anzalone interception— His second of the day and third of the season. One more field goal off of an Alex Anzalone interception and the Buccaneers expanded their lead. 6-0, Tampa Bay. Second Quarter: The difference between the start of the game’s first quarter and its second? Not much. More rain and more Micheal Penix interceptions. For the start of quarter number two, Penix, under pressure from Rueben Bain Jr., decided to spread the wealth tossing a fourth down interception to Jacob Parrish. Back on the field after another turnover, Tampa Bay’s offense stayed consistent. Run, run, run, and run. The Buccaneers’ only pass attempt of the drive would actually wind up as a rush attempt as well after Baker Mayfield scooped up his third fumble of the day and scurried forward for a short gain. Tampa’s first drive of the second quarter ended with 4:04 left in the half and three more points on the scoreboard. 9-0, Buccaneers. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coming off of a running bonanza against Carolina for their second win of the season, week eight was set to feature more running, a downpour, and no Baker Mayfield glove. Would a second consecutive game of relentless running by the Buccaneers’ offense be enough for the Buccaneers to climb out of their early season hole and to the top of the NFC South? First Quarter: It was Todd Bowles’ defense up first on Sunday. Battling on a water-logged field, Tampa’s strongest unit took the field and bent a bit, however, there was no break. The Falcons pushed into Tampa territory before ultimately needing to settle for a long field goal attempt. Weather conditions not favoring Nick Folk, the kick was missed and missed badly. Converting turnovers into points or this case missed field goals into points gave Tampa the first lead of the day. 3-0, Buccaneers. The response from the Falcons was quite mild, an interception by Alex Anzalone. Penix looking for Drake London on a slant, found Anzalone for his second interception of the season. Turnovers into points would fail Tampa on their next drive— Bucky Ivring, breaking into space on a broken play, was met by Jessie Bates at the goal line for a 2023 Antoine Winfield Jr.-esque forced fumble stripping the ball out at the goal line which rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Rest assured, Tampa’s defense understood the assignment. Back on the field, following an Alex Anzalone pick that didn’t result into points, fans watched Michael Penix drop back and throw another Alex Anzalone interception— His second of the day and third of the season. One more field goal off of an Alex Anzalone interception and the Buccaneers expanded their lead. 6-0, Tampa Bay. Second Quarter: The difference between the start of the game’s first quarter and its second? Not much. More rain and more Micheal Penix interceptions. For the start of quarter number two, Penix, under pressure from Rueben Bain Jr., decided to spread the wealth tossing a fourth down interception to Jacob Parrish. Back on the field after another turnover, Tampa Bay’s offense stayed consistent. Run, run, run, and run. The Buccaneers’ only pass attempt of the drive would actually wind up as a rush attempt as well after Baker Mayfield scooped up his third fumble of the day and scurried forward for a short gain. Tampa’s first drive of the second quarter ended with 4:04 left in the half and three more points on the scoreboard. 9-0, Buccaneers. The Bucs and Falcons would each exchange run-first, slow-paced, non-scoring drive to close out half number one and head to the intermission— The only first half since 1978 to feature less than three completed passes. Third Quarter: With zero first half completions and a two-score lead, Baker Mayfield was under center at the 30 yard line to start the third quarter— Run, run, third down drop, and a punt. Tampa Bay, still repping their signature no completion streak, sent their defense back out onto the field for another three-and-out stop. The third quarter was nothing but rain and punts until the final five minutes. Bucky Irving ripped through Atlanta’s defense for a 45 yard rush— Two plays later, it was Kenny Gainwell’s turn. Gainwell, with his second break away run in as many weeks, put the Buccaneers inside the 10 yard line. It would be another two plays until Bucky Irving put the Bucs inside the end zone. 16-0, Tampa Bay. Fourth Quarter: The Falcons seized some bits of momentum in the waning moments of the third quarter. With the final quarter beginning at the Tampa Bay 30 yard line and an Atlanta decision. Neglecting a short field goal the Falcons opted for a forth down attempted and converted with a Michael Penix tush push. Unfortunately for Falcons’ fans, the team would ask Penix to throw next and he would once again throw to a Tampa Bay defender. Penix’s fourth interception would be tossed to Zyon McCollum. Atlanta’s next bite at the apple would be from their 12 yard with just over seven minutes to go— Three-and-out. Tampa’s response— Three-and-out. Backed up from their own two, Michael Penix found Atlanta’s biggest spark of the day— Jahan Dotson for 76 yards. Dotson’s catch and run was the only chink Todd Bowles’ armor, the Falcons’ drive was immediately stalled afterwards and the Buccaneers salted away the rest of the clock and the game. Tampa Bay, despite their 0-4 start, is 3-5 and very much in contention of the NFC South.

item.title: Illinois gets two players back for season opener, but Mirkovic suffers another setback
item.description: Illinois basketball will get some much-needed reinforcements for Monday night’s season opener against Fairleigh Dickinson, but the injury news isn’t all positive for the Fighting Illini. Head coach Brad Underwood confirmed Sunday that both Andrej Stojakovic and Zvonimir Ivisic will be active and in the lineup when Illinois opens its regular season at State Farm Center. Both players suffered injuries during Illinois’ exhibition loss to Baylor last month. Stojakovic and Ivisic each took hard falls and appeared to hit their heads, forcing them to leave the game. Neither played in Illinois’ final exhibition against UIC. There was less encouraging news regarding sophomore forward David Mirkovic. Underwood revealed Sunday that Mirkovic underwent an emergency appendectomy Saturday night after developing appendicitis. His appendix was removed, and he will not play Monday. Mirkovic was already recovering from offseason foot surgery that has kept him out of all three exhibition games. The preseason All-American had recently been spotted working out without his walking boot before returning to the boot and scooter during Illinois’ exhibition against Baylor. Underwood did not provide a timetable for Mirkovic’s return. Freshman guard Lincoln Williams also remains questionable for Monday’s opener. Underwood has not provided an indication of whether Williams will be available. Illinois opens its season against Fairleigh Dickinson at 7 p.m. Monday at State Farm Center.

item.title: I'll tell my players to dive in future - Iraola
item.description: Andoni Iraola says that he will tell his players to go down in future after Liverpool were denied a penalty in Sunday's defeat by Arsenal. With Liverpool trailing 1-0 after Kai Havertz's opener, Alexander Isak's shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber in the first half as he went for a header from Bradley Barcola's cross. However, the Liverpool striker stayed on his feet and referee Andy Madley did not point to the spot. Stuart Attwell, on video assistant referee (VAR) duty, determined that there was not enough in the tug for the decision to be overturned, but Iraola disagreed. "There is a clear grab of the shirt," the Spaniard told Match of the Day. "Alex [Isak] was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he grabbed the shirt. "If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100%. It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it." On what the answer is going forward, Iraola added: "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it." Isak turned and spoke to Timber after the incident, but did not appeal to the referee after staying on his feet. Iraola told Sky Sports that going forward, managers should tell their players to go to the floor. On if he will tell Isak that going forward, he added: "Yes, definitely." He elaborated in his news conference when asked by BBC Sport if he would have to tell his players to be more smart, going forward. "It's a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them, go down, because they're not going to call it otherwise. And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don't go down, you don't call it. Then it's like, no, you are all the time going down," said Iraola. "But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away that there is a clear, clear pull." The understanding is that because there was minimal contact and it was a slight tug on the shirt, rather than a sustained holding offence, the play was allowed to continue. Iraola conceded in his news conference that "it is not going to change anything" if Pro Ref, the Premier League's refereeing body, was to offer an apology about the incident. Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC Sport: "Timber takes a huge risk by grabbing the shirt. It could easily have been given on another day. "It's right on the limit. It has to be sustained holding - some will say it was sustained, some will say it wasn't. But it's interesting that Isak didn't even appeal." Liverpool also had another penalty appeal turned waved away when Cody Gakpo went down in the box under pressure from Christos Tzolis. Liverpool also had another penalty appeal turned waved away when Cody Gakpo went down in the box under pressure from Christos Tzolis. 'It's an odd reaction from Isak' Liverpool did not have any shots on target against Arsenal [Getty Images] Former Liverpool midfielder Danny Murphy said the decision came at a pivotal point in the game. "I think Arsenal got lucky," he told Match of the Day. "If Isak maybe makes a bit more of it. I hate to see players exaggerate, but he's going to score. It's a big moment in the game "I feel for the referee because it happened so quickly. I thought there was enough for VAR to have another look and give him another look. Gary Neville agreed that, for a centre-forward, it was an unusual reaction from Isak, who failed to connect with the ball due to the pull. "When you get pulled and you're just about to score a goal, you normally complain like crazy. It'd a very odd reaction from Isak not to react." Asked if Isak should have reacted more, Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk said: "We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras. Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal." item.title: 5 Classic Nintendo Games That Are So Good They Never Need a Remake
item.description: Video games have been around for so many decades that the next time you sit down to play one, you’ll have tens of thousands of terrific options to choose from. A lot of us find ourselves playing newer releases when the time rolls around, because older titles have slipped from our minds. But they can also provide ample entertainment, if we give them a chance.

item.title: Video: UFC fighter’s 18-year-old brother scores brutal 1st-round knockout in LFA debut
item.description: It apparently runs in the Bahomondes’ family. In his LFA debut, 18-year-old prospect Alberth Bahomondes followed in his brother Ignacio Bahomondes’ footsteps by delivering a blistering finish over Joey Hart in the first round. 18-year-old Alberth Bahamondes (8-1) makes his LFA debut with a vicious first round KO. Good lord. Ignacio's little bro may be a problem. #LFA45 pic.twitter.com/ZDcGhvcpsy — caposa (@Grabaka_Hitman) October 31, 2026 With both fighters willing to stand and bang, Hart threw an overhand right that got Bahomondes’ attention but it didn’t deter him from continuing to step into the exchanges. That’s when Bahomondes jumped into a beautifully timed combination capped off by a devastating overhand right that put Hart on the canvas. It only took a few more shots for the referee to see enough to rush in to stop the fight with Bahomondes getting the first round knockout. Despite his young age, Bahomondes — who has finishes in every single victory — is already 8-1 in his career, and with his third win in a row, he may not be far from joining his brother Ignacio in the UFC.

item.title: Yankees Social Media Spotlight: Halloween Edition
item.description: NEW YORK, NY - OCTOBER 07: A general view of Yankee Stadium during Game Three of the American League Division Series presented by Booking.com between the Tampa Bay Rays and the New York Yankees on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by Michael Urakami/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images It’s Sunday once more, and you know what that means — it’s time for our weekly social media roundup! The 2026 season has come to a close, with Gary Sánchez and the Milwaukee Brewers defeating the Tampa Bay Rays to secure the third straight World Series trophy for the National League (and fifth of the decade). And now, for all 30 teams, the cold winter of the offseason is upon us — one that will be longer than normal due to the impending lockout. The offseason doesn’t mean that life stops, however, and this week, we have a jam-packed social media roundup. And so, without further ado, let’s get started! Happy Halloween! Being the last day of October, yesterday was, of course, Halloween. Naturally, the Yankees family got in on the festivities. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram None of this, though, beats how Spencer Jones spent his Halloweekend: getting engaged at the top of the Empire State Building. View this post on Instagram Looking Back As has been the case over the last few weeks, several players — and their families — took to social media to reflect on the past season…and, in the case of former Yankee Shane Greene, to reflect on his career. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram On the Road Again Normally, I don’t like posting things that are, in truth, embedded ads, but I figured this one might be important to know. Yankees starter Will Warren is heading south for the winter, and while he didn’t explicitly say where he’s going to spend the next few months, I wouldn’t be surprised to see a bunch of players getting apartments/homes near each other for the winter; that way, if spring training doesn’t start on time, they will be near others that they can work out/train with. View this post on Instagram Family Time The Sabathia clan descended on the University of Michigan for Parents’ Weekend. View this post on Instagram Between that and following the Brewers’ quest to snap their long title drought, it’s been a busy month for our old pal CC. Although he only spent half a (highly memorable!) season in Milwaukee, he’s always felt a strong connection with the city—especially the late Bob Uecker—and was overjoyed to see them win it all. Sabathia was at several games of the Brew Crew’s championship run. Meanwhile, the Cole family had dinner, courtesy of Chef Gerrit. View this post on Instagram Clarke Schmidt headed out into the woods with his family, where he caught a fish! item.content:encoded: NEW YORK, NY - OCTOBER 07: A general view of Yankee Stadium during Game Three of the American League Division Series presented by Booking.com between the Tampa Bay Rays and the New York Yankees on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 in New York, New York. (Photo by Michael Urakami/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images It’s Sunday once more, and you know what that means — it’s time for our weekly social media roundup! The 2026 season has come to a close, with Gary Sánchez and the Milwaukee Brewers defeating the Tampa Bay Rays to secure the third straight World Series trophy for the National League (and fifth of the decade). And now, for all 30 teams, the cold winter of the offseason is upon us — one that will be longer than normal due to the impending lockout. The offseason doesn’t mean that life stops, however, and this week, we have a jam-packed social media roundup. And so, without further ado, let’s get started! Happy Halloween! Being the last day of October, yesterday was, of course, Halloween. Naturally, the Yankees family got in on the festivities. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram None of this, though, beats how Spencer Jones spent his Halloweekend: getting engaged at the top of the Empire State Building. View this post on Instagram Looking Back As has been the case over the last few weeks, several players — and their families — took to social media to reflect on the past season…and, in the case of former Yankee Shane Greene, to reflect on his career. View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram View this post on Instagram On the Road Again Normally, I don’t like posting things that are, in truth, embedded ads, but I figured this one might be important to know. Yankees starter Will Warren is heading south for the winter, and while he didn’t explicitly say where he’s going to spend the next few months, I wouldn’t be surprised to see a bunch of players getting apartments/homes near each other for the winter; that way, if spring training doesn’t start on time, they will be near others that they can work out/train with. View this post on Instagram Family Time The Sabathia clan descended on the University of Michigan for Parents’ Weekend. View this post on Instagram Between that and following the Brewers’ quest to snap their long title drought, it’s been a busy month for our old pal CC. Although he only spent half a (highly memorable!) season in Milwaukee, he’s always felt a strong connection with the city—especially the late Bob Uecker—and was overjoyed to see them win it all. Sabathia was at several games of the Brew Crew’s championship run. Meanwhile, the Cole family had dinner, courtesy of Chef Gerrit. View this post on Instagram Clarke Schmidt headed out into the woods with his family, where he caught a fish! View this post on Instagram The Pride of Somerset The Somerset Patriots, as always, take great pride in the big league performance of their former players; this week, they celebrated the Cy Young performance of a certain Cam Schlittler. View this post on Instagram Award Season Yankee pitcher David Cone was named the recipient of the 2026 Curt Flood Award for his “longtime devotion to the MLBPA.” Congratulations, Coney!

item.title: Should Brian Fariñas start at right-back for Barcelona against Aston Villa?
item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Hansi Flick was forced into a few creative changes at the back in Satuday’s dominant La Liga win over Alavés, and while Frenkie de Jong’s performance at center-back has been the subject of plenty of attention, Brian Fariñas’ display at right-back cannot be overlooked. The 20-year-old midfielder made his debut for the first team out of position but had a very good night, looking comfortable in the role and making smart contributions in attack with his overlapping runs and passes into the final third. His defense was also solid, and Fariñas is definitely in contention to remain in the lineup for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Aston Villa at Camp Nou. The status of Jules Kounde remains uncertain as of now and Flick could also go with a more traditional full-back duo of João Cancelo and Alejandro Balde, but Fariñas’ name cannot be discarded. So today’s Barca Blaugranes Question of the Day is: Should Brian Fariñas start at right-back against Aston Villa? Now it’s over to you! Feel free to share your thoughts, opinions and answers in the comments section below!

item.title: Gary Neville Hails Arsenal’s “Defensive Masterclass” After Historic Anfield Victory
item.description: Gary Neville Hails Arsenal’s “Defensive Masterclass” After Historic Anfield Victory Gary Neville was full of praise for Arsenal’s defensive performance after Mikel Arteta’s side secured a historic 1-0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday evening. Kai Havertz’s 16th-minute goal proved decisive as the Gunners ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Liverpool’s ground, moving three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But while Havertz will deservedly take the headlines for his winning goal, it was Arsenal’s collective defensive display that particularly impressed the former Manchester United defender. Neville Praises Arsenal’s Defensive Organisation Speaking during Sky Sports ‘ coverage of the match, Neville delivered a glowing assessment of Arsenal’s defensive performance. “It’s been a defensive masterclass from Arsenal,” Neville declared. It was a remarkable achievement against a Liverpool side desperate to get back into the contest after falling behind early. The hosts enjoyed extended spells of possession and registered 17 attempts on goal, yet struggled to create clear opportunities against Arteta’s well-organised defence. Florian Wirtz struck the crossbar with a free-kick, while Alexis Mac Allister missed a promising headed opportunity, but Arsenal largely restricted Liverpool to efforts that failed to seriously trouble David Raya. Gabriel and Ezri Konsa were particularly important in the heart of Arsenal’s defence, with Declan Rice providing further protection in midfield. The determination and discipline on display demonstrated why Arsenal have become such difficult opponents to break down. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Arsenal Send Another Message to Their Title Rivals What makes Neville’s assessment particularly significant is the importance of the occasion. Arsenal had not won a Premier League match at Anfield since September 2012, when Arteta himself was still playing for the Gunners. As we discussed in our confirmed Arsenal team announcement ahead of the Liverpool clash , Arteta had several important selection decisions to make, particularly following the disappointing Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town. His players responded with a performance built on discipline, resilience and the ability to take their opportunity when it arrived. It was also an encouraging response from Havertz, whose recent form had attracted questions . Manchester City’s defeat to Brighton on Saturday had presented Arsenal with a tremendous opportunity, and they took full advantage. There will undoubtedly be more spectacular attacking performances this season, but victories like this could prove just as important when the title race reaches its conclusion. Neville’s verdict underlines something Arsenal supporters have increasingly recognised. This is a team capable of winning difficult matches through defensive strength as well as attacking quality. item.title: Michigan drops two spots in ESPN’s SP+ rankings after beating Rutgers
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 31: Wide receiver Salesi Moa #12 of the Michigan Wolverines runs with the ball after a catch chased by Defensive back Devonte Anderson #21 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first quarter at SHI Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Mark Smith/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Michigan once again didn’t turn in a clean performance on Saturday, defeating Rutgers by a 28-21 final score despite being favored by more than two touchdowns. As such, Michigan found itself dropping two spots in the latest edition of ESPN and Bill Connelly’s SP+ rankings, now sitting at No. 29. For those of you who might be new to SP+, it’s an advanced metric that takes into account a team’s offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the “average” college football team by on a neutral field. In other words, it’s a metric designed to look at how “good” teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes. Michigan’s rating is 11.5 after Week 9, meaning that it would beat an “average” college football team by 11.5 points. The Wolverines flipped the script a bit against Rutgers, with their defense having something of a letdown while the offense looked a bit better. Still, SP+ has Michigan’s offense as the No. 87-ranked nationally and the defense as the No. 4-ranked nationally. The Wolverines still have four games left on their schedule this season, with three of their opponents — Oregon, UCLA, and Ohio State — all ranked higher. That means that Michigan would be predicted to finish the regular season at 6-6. Looking ahead to next week, Michigan will square off against a 2-6 Michigan State team in the Battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy. Michigan will be going for its fifth straight victory over its in-state rival, which ranks as the No. 85 team in SP+ with a rating of -3.1. That means that the Wolverines are predicted to win by about two touchdowns and will get the advantage of playing on their home field as well. We’ll see how things pan out when the teams take the field at 7:30 p.m. at the Big House on Saturday.

item.title: Coaching friends become foes when Siena basketball opens at Bryant
item.description: Siena head coach Nevada Smith during the first official day of men's basketball practice on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) On his way to becoming the new Siena men's basketball coach, Nevada Smith got an assist from former Saints head coach Jamion Christian. Christian made a phone call in 2020 to recommend Smith to then-Texas coach Shaka Smart, who hired Smith as his director of program development. Smith worked for Smart for six years during stops at Texas and Marquette until Siena hired Smith last April. "I've known Jamion a long time," Smith said. "I have a lot of respect for him." They'll meet again Monday night when Siena faces Bryant University in the opener in Smithfield, R.I. While Smith is making his regular-season debut as a Division I head coach, Christian is entering his second season as Bulldogs head coach. "I'm glad that this thing has kind of come full circle and we get a chance to compete against each other a little bit," said Christian, who led Siena in 2018-19. Smith visited a Siena practice during Christian's lone season in Loudonville. At the time, Smith was the head coach for the NBA G League's Sioux Falls Skyforce, an affiliate of the Miami Heat. Smith lived in Saratoga Springs with his wife during the offseason. When Smith was head coach at Division III Keystone College in Pennsylvania in 2012-13, he made the three-hour drive to watch practice at Mount St. Mary's, where Christian was in his first season as head coach. Christian already had ties to Smart. He was an assistant under Smart at Virginia Commonwealth University in 2011-12. Years later, Smith asked Christian to make a call to Smart on his behalf about the Texas opening. "I'm really happy for (Smith)," Christian said. "To see someone have this kind of rise, I think, is really special. I know he'll do a great job there at Siena and carry that legacy and do it with a lot of pride." Smith and Christian were together for a season at Marquette in 2022-23, the year that Christian was out of coaching after being fired by George Washington. While Smith was a special assistant to Smart, Christian served as a consultant for the Golden Eagles, who won the Big East championship that season. "It'll be fun to play against (Christian) and play against his team," Smith said. "I know he'll do a great job." Bryant went 9-22 last year in Christian's debut season, which began with an 82-66 loss to Siena at MVP Arena. The Bulldogs were picked to finish fifth in the America East Conference preseason coaches poll released in September. "I'm always optimistic, people would say, but I do think this team has championship-level quality to it," Christian said. item.content:encoded: Siena head coach Nevada Smith during the first official day of men's basketball practice on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026, in Colonie, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) On his way to becoming the new Siena men's basketball coach, Nevada Smith got an assist from former Saints head coach Jamion Christian. Christian made a phone call in 2020 to recommend Smith to then-Texas coach Shaka Smart, who hired Smith as his director of program development. Smith worked for Smart for six years during stops at Texas and Marquette until Siena hired Smith last April. "I've known Jamion a long time," Smith said. "I have a lot of respect for him." They'll meet again Monday night when Siena faces Bryant University in the opener in Smithfield, R.I. While Smith is making his regular-season debut as a Division I head coach, Christian is entering his second season as Bulldogs head coach. "I'm glad that this thing has kind of come full circle and we get a chance to compete against each other a little bit," said Christian, who led Siena in 2018-19. Smith visited a Siena practice during Christian's lone season in Loudonville. At the time, Smith was the head coach for the NBA G League's Sioux Falls Skyforce, an affiliate of the Miami Heat. Smith lived in Saratoga Springs with his wife during the offseason. When Smith was head coach at Division III Keystone College in Pennsylvania in 2012-13, he made the three-hour drive to watch practice at Mount St. Mary's, where Christian was in his first season as head coach. Christian already had ties to Smart. He was an assistant under Smart at Virginia Commonwealth University in 2011-12. Years later, Smith asked Christian to make a call to Smart on his behalf about the Texas opening. "I'm really happy for (Smith)," Christian said. "To see someone have this kind of rise, I think, is really special. I know he'll do a great job there at Siena and carry that legacy and do it with a lot of pride." Smith and Christian were together for a season at Marquette in 2022-23, the year that Christian was out of coaching after being fired by George Washington. While Smith was a special assistant to Smart, Christian served as a consultant for the Golden Eagles, who won the Big East championship that season. "It'll be fun to play against (Christian) and play against his team," Smith said. "I know he'll do a great job." Bryant went 9-22 last year in Christian's debut season, which began with an 82-66 loss to Siena at MVP Arena. The Bulldogs were picked to finish fifth in the America East Conference preseason coaches poll released in September. "I'm always optimistic, people would say, but I do think this team has championship-level quality to it," Christian said. Bryant returns 6-11 graduate forward Keegan Harvey, named preseason all-conference, and sophomore combination guard Ty Tabales, who made the all-rookie team last season. During the offseason, Christian added Georgia Tech transfer Eric Chatfield Jr., a 6-foot sophomore guard whom Christian said "has a chance to be Player of the Year in the league." He also brought in former St. Bonaventure wing Duane Thompson, who will be the sixth man. Other newcomers are 6-9 sophomore transfer Onyx Nnani from South Florida and former New Haven guard Andre Pasha. Christian said he and Smith share some of the same basketball values, though Smith is more influenced by the pro game. "We both believe in scoring quickly and shooting a lot of 3s," Christian said. "We'll get a chance to learn what he values on the defensive side of it." Monday will mark the first real Division I game for Siena freshman Tim Ibukunoluwa, who had 23 points and 14 rebounds in an 81-76 exhibition loss to Syracuse at MVP Arena on Oct. 18. However, Ibukunoluwa didn't think that encouraging performance in front of a large crowd against a big-name opponent means much going into Monday's opener. "I think to us it really doesn't matter," he said. "It's just another game. It wasn't a proper game. That's what exhibitions are for. I feel like this is the real test against Bryant on Monday." Siena will begin pursuit of a second straight Metro Conference title. They won the title last year under Gerry McNamara, who departed to become head coach at Syracuse. "We're really excited to get out there," Smith said. "We continue to grow since our last public appearance a couple of Sundays ago, so I'm excited to see what we can do." This ends Siena and Bryant's contract, which began before Smith or Christian were hired. If the series doesn't continue, Christian said, he could see Siena and Bryant meeting in closed scrimmages every year. Subscribe There’s more to Albany with the Times Union. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at Coaching friends become foes when Siena basketball opens at Bryant .

item.title: Sensational playmaker who plays like Philippe Coutinho is coming to Liverpool
item.description: Sensational playmaker who plays like Philippe Coutinho is coming to Liverpool Liverpool have agreed a deal and have secured their new Philippe Coutinho in the process. The Brazilian was simply a sensation footballer. His Liverpool exit left a bitter taste there is no denying that, but looking back, it's difficult to begrudge him for that decision. The money the Reds received from Barcelona also helped fund the arrivals of Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, so it's fair to say Liverpool got a pretty good deal out of it. Barcelona, perhaps, not so much. Still, with a bit of hindsight, you can really appreciate just how special Coutinho was. The Brazilian was an absolute magician, a natural no.10 who made the game look effortless. He could glide past defenders, pick a pass that nobody else saw and unlock even the tightest of defences. His vision and technical ability were right up there with the best, and he always seemed to know exactly where his teammates were. When Coutinho was at his best, there weren't many players who could match the kind of creativity and magic he brought to the pitch. Florian Wirtz is struggling to be Liverpool's next Coutinho When the Reds spent all that money on the German, it felt like for the first time in many years, Liverpool had discovered the heir to Coutinho's throne. But Wirtz has struggled to adapt to English football. Unlike, Coutinho who settled in with ease Wirtz isn't yet catching the eye. He seems to be a little off pace, a little indecisive and just not the player we saw take the Bundesliga by storm over the course of his young career. How to unlock him remains the biggest mystery in Iraola's career. It could also determine the success of the Spaniard's time at Anfield. Things are getting better but there is no denying Wirtz could yet reach another level. Behind the scenes, Liverpool might have an alternative solution. Meet Liverpool's next Coutinho - Erik Farkas The Reds had two priorities to sort out this summer. Liverpool regard Joshua Abe and Erik Farkas as two of their biggest talents. Both attracted the interest of a host of clubs from England and abroad. But both Liverpool have now managed to secure an agreement with to sign a professional contract. Abe agreed his over the summer, and Liverpool confirmed they had agreed a deal with Farkas on Friday. This is a huge deal for the Reds. Farkas has that Coutinho quality about him. He can unlock any defence, he is blessed with a fantastic football IQ and a great vision and technical quality. Like Coutinho he's mastered those through balls with the outside of his foot. He is a pure magician and a sheer joy to watch. And thankfully Liverpool have managed to sign his services for the foreseeable future. Soon, he will be coming to join the first-team, too. Farkas already has six goals and three assists in just 553 minutes of football at academy level this season.

item.title: Palmeiras beat Vasco to move closer to the Copa do Brasil final 🇧🇷
item.description: Palmeiras beat Vasco to move closer to the Copa do Brasil final 🇧🇷 Palmeiras beat Vasco 1–0 at Nubank Park, taking an important step toward a place in the Copa do Brasil final. Maurício scored the only goal on Sunday (1) in the first leg of the semifinal. The match was marked by TWO controversies, with Vasco players protesting a penalty that was not awarded and a sending-off. What's next 🏆 The return leg between Vasco and Palmeiras will take place next Sunday (8), at 5 p.m., at São Januário. A draw will be enough for Palmeiras. Vasco need to win by at least two goals. A one-goal win for the Giant of the Hill (1–0, 2–1, 3–2...) will send the tie to penalties. The winner will face Atlético-MG or Grêmio on Sunday, December 6, at Mané Garrincha. First half 🔍 Palmeiras started better and controlled proceedings for the first 30 minutes. Giay even missed an open goal. The hosts' dominance paid off in the 24th minute. Maurício received a pass from Marlon Freitas and fired into the corner. Palmeiras eased off, and the game became feisty. The referee showed FOUR yellow cards—three of them to Vasco. Second half 🔍 The second half featured TWO controversies. Vasco players appealed for a penalty after a handball by Barboza in the box. Then, in the 77th minute, Saldívia was shown a red card, leaving Vasco down to 10 men. Did it warrant a second yellow? Watch the footage from GE and have your say! Palmeiras continued to dominate possession (61%) but, despite their numerical advantage, their final ball let them down and they could not extend their lead. But first, the Brasileirão 🇧🇷 Both clubs have fixtures in the 34th round of the Brasileirão before the semifinal return leg. Palmeiras (second with 70 points) will host Remo on Thursday (5), at 7:30 p.m., at Nubank Park. Vasco (13th with 38 points) will visit Athletico on Wednesday (4), at 7:30 p.m., at Arena da Baixada. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

The match was marked by TWO controversies, with Vasco players protesting a penalty that was not awarded and a sending-off. What's next 🏆 The return leg between Vasco and Palmeiras will take place next Sunday (8), at 5 p.m., at São Januário. A draw will be enough for Palmeiras. Vasco need to win by at least two goals. A one-goal win for the Giant of the Hill (1–0, 2–1, 3–2...) will send the tie to penalties. The winner will face Atlético-MG or Grêmio on Sunday, December 6, at Mané Garrincha. First half 🔍 Palmeiras started better and controlled proceedings for the first 30 minutes. Giay even missed an open goal. The hosts' dominance paid off in the 24th minute. Maurício received a pass from Marlon Freitas and fired into the corner. Palmeiras eased off, and the game became feisty. The referee showed FOUR yellow cards—three of them to Vasco. Second half 🔍 The second half featured TWO controversies. Vasco players appealed for a penalty after a handball by Barboza in the box. Then, in the 77th minute, Saldívia was shown a red card, leaving Vasco down to 10 men. Did it warrant a second yellow? Watch the footage from GE and have your say! Palmeiras continued to dominate possession (61%) but, despite their numerical advantage, their final ball let them down and they could not extend their lead. But first, the Brasileirão 🇧🇷 Both clubs have fixtures in the 34th round of the Brasileirão before the semifinal return leg. Palmeiras (second with 70 points) will host Remo on Thursday (5), at 7:30 p.m., at Nubank Park. Vasco (13th with 38 points) will visit Athletico on Wednesday (4), at 7:30 p.m., at Arena da Baixada. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

item.title: Picture: Furious Inter ultras slam players after derby defeat
item.description: Picture: Furious Inter ultras slam players after derby defeat Inter ultras put up a banner after a 3-1 loss against Milan, criticising the players’ attitude during and after the game: ‘A derby lost without even playing. Not even the guts to say goodbye.’ Inter lost their first Serie A game of the season on Saturday, falling 3-1 to city rivals Milan. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Fans of FC Internazionale during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Although it was only Inter’s first Serie A defeat in 2026-27, their ultras didn’t like the team’s attitude or that the players left the pitch without waving to the supporters in Curva Nord. “A derby lost without even playing. Not even the guts to say goodbye,” Inter ultras wrote on a banner which they placed just outside San Siro. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Djed Spence of FC Internazionale in action during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Lazio’s Sunday victory means Inter now sit second in the Serie A table, three points behind the Biancocelesti. Inter ultras blame players after 3-1 derby loss vs. Milan – Picture La delusione per il derby perso si è trasformata in una presa di posizione molto dura da parte della Curva Nord. Dopo la sconfitta contro il Milan, è comparso uno striscione dal messaggio inequivocabile: «Un derby perso senza giocare. Neanche le palle di salutare». Poche parole, ma sufficienti a raccontare il malcontento di una parte della tifoseria nerazzurra. Nel mirino non c’è soltanto il risultato, ma soprattutto l’atteggiamento mostrato dalla squadra e quanto accaduto al termine della partita. Una contestazione che riaccende il confronto tra squadra e tifosi e che testimonia quanto possa pesare una sconfitta in una partita così sentita. Il derby, ancora una volta, lascia strascichi che vanno ben oltre i novanta minuti.

item.title: New Astros GM Randy Flores helped build the Cardinals' farm system. A closer look at his draft record
item.description: JJ Wetherholt, drafted in 2024, is arguably the best first-round success story from new Astros general manager Randy Flores' time running the Cardinals' drafts. (Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) In the Houston Astros ' news release Friday announcing the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager , club owner Jim Crane's statement noted that the Astros were impressed during the interview process "with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition." Flores joined the St. Louis Cardinals' front office in August 2015 as scouting director and continued to oversee the Cardinals' amateur drafts after being promoted to assistant general manager in late 2018. His most recent title in St. Louis was assistant GM of amateur and pro acquisition. Flores' duties with St. Louis evidently went beyond just the amateur draft. He was overseeing both the Cardinals' amateur and pro scouting efforts, per the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, and The Athletic reported that Flores was involved in major-league operations including the trade deadline. Nor are the results of 11 drafts Flores led for the Cardinals a precise way to forecast how he will fare in his first crack at running a baseball operations department. Still, Crane's appraisal invites a look at St. Louis' track record of drafts and farm system strength during Flores' time there. The Astros are bringing in Flores at a pivotal juncture . Their regular-season win total has declined in four consecutive years, their core is aging and their minor-league system is ranked among the sport's thinnest by outside evaluations. For a franchise that has resisted long-term deals, strengthening the latter does appear a key part of sustaining the contending window Crane has vowed will not close during his tenure. The draft is a notoriously inexact science, and whether picks pan out can be heavily impacted afterward by player development. Scouting and player acquisition in broad terms may also extend to international signings or players added in trades or free agency. Both are caveats to this examination. Overall farm system strength may be an area to start. From 2016 through 2023, the Cardinals' system ranked between ninth and 14th out of 30 teams in Baseball America's preseason rankings in each year except one. It then dipped to 20th in 2024 and ranked 18th in 2025. Starting in 2025, the Cardinals entered a kind of rebuild, reducing major-league payroll and reportedly investing more in player development and technology. They reduced payroll further in 2026, largely by trading away veterans on larger contracts before the season. St. Louis' farm system climbed to No. 2 in the Baseball America preseason rankings this year, with its highest-rated prospects mainly a mix of players acquired in those trades last offseason and selections from its recent drafts.
