item.content:encoded: JJ Wetherholt, drafted in 2024, is arguably the best first-round success story from new Astros general manager Randy Flores' time running the Cardinals' drafts. (Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) In the Houston Astros ' news release Friday announcing the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager , club owner Jim Crane's statement noted that the Astros were impressed during the interview process "with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition." Flores joined the St. Louis Cardinals' front office in August 2015 as scouting director and continued to oversee the Cardinals' amateur drafts after being promoted to assistant general manager in late 2018. His most recent title in St. Louis was assistant GM of amateur and pro acquisition. Flores' duties with St. Louis evidently went beyond just the amateur draft. He was overseeing both the Cardinals' amateur and pro scouting efforts, per the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, and The Athletic reported that Flores was involved in major-league operations including the trade deadline. Nor are the results of 11 drafts Flores led for the Cardinals a precise way to forecast how he will fare in his first crack at running a baseball operations department. Still, Crane's appraisal invites a look at St. Louis' track record of drafts and farm system strength during Flores' time there. The Astros are bringing in Flores at a pivotal juncture . Their regular-season win total has declined in four consecutive years, their core is aging and their minor-league system is ranked among the sport's thinnest by outside evaluations. For a franchise that has resisted long-term deals, strengthening the latter does appear a key part of sustaining the contending window Crane has vowed will not close during his tenure. The draft is a notoriously inexact science, and whether picks pan out can be heavily impacted afterward by player development. Scouting and player acquisition in broad terms may also extend to international signings or players added in trades or free agency. Both are caveats to this examination. Overall farm system strength may be an area to start. From 2016 through 2023, the Cardinals' system ranked between ninth and 14th out of 30 teams in Baseball America's preseason rankings in each year except one. It then dipped to 20th in 2024 and ranked 18th in 2025. Starting in 2025, the Cardinals entered a kind of rebuild, reducing major-league payroll and reportedly investing more in player development and technology. They reduced payroll further in 2026, largely by trading away veterans on larger contracts before the season. St. Louis' farm system climbed to No. 2 in the Baseball America preseason rankings this year, with its highest-rated prospects mainly a mix of players acquired in those trades last offseason and selections from its recent drafts. From 2016-23, their first eight drafts under Flores, the Cardinals never picked higher than No. 18. They forfeited their top two picks in 2017 , as well, as a punishment for former scouting director Chris Correa illegally accessing the Astros' computer database . Related or not, many of the Cardinals' draft successes to this point under Flores stemmed from middle rounds. St. Louis made 14 first-round selections from 2016-26. Of those, shortstop JJ Wetherholt, who was taken with the No. 7 overall pick in 2024 and debuted in 2026, has already accrued the most wins above replacement, per Baseball Reference, with 4.5 bWAR. That reflects some early misses. Jordan Walker, the Cardinals' first-round pick in 2020, made the All-Star team in a breakout 2026 season, though, illustrating how draft evaluations may evolve with time. The shortened 2020 draft could prove particularly fruitful for St. Louis, as the second round yielded Masyn Winn, the Kingwood High school alumnus and its current shortstop, and Alec Burleson, who led the majors in RBIs this season. In 2016, the Cardinals drafted pitcher Zac Gallen in the third round and infielder Tommy Edman in the sixth. Edman has accrued 20.7 bWAR in the majors, to this point the most of any player drafted under Flores. Gallen, who was traded as a minor-leaguer in a package for slugger Marcell Ozuna, is second at 19 bWAR, all accrued with other clubs. In 2018, the Cardinals selected Brendan Donovan in the seventh round and Lars Nootbaar in the eighth. Donovan became an All-Star with St. Louis and was among the players traded last winter, garnering the Cardinals a haul of prospects and draft picks. Nootbaar became part of the Cardinals' outfield and was their longest-tenured position player when he was traded at this year's deadline. With no playoff appearances since 2022, the Cardinals drafted seventh overall in 2024, fifth overall in 2025 - selecting pitcher Liam Doyle - and five times in the first two rounds in 2026. Wetherholt, their first-rounder in 2024, is the only player from those three classes who has played in the majors at this point, so a full appraisal of later drafts under Flores won't be apparent for years. In total, players drafted by the Cardinals from 2016-24 have combined for 112.7 bWAR in the majors. As a comparison, players drafted by the Astros in that same stretch have accrued 49.1 bWAR. The latter number reflects Houston's issues in the draft over the past decade. The Astros forfeited their top two picks in 2020 and '21 as punishment for the franchise's sign-stealing scandal , but other early selections have gone unrealized. Since 2016, players drafted in the first round by the Astros have totaled minus-1.1 bWAR in the majors, while their second-round picks have combined for minus-2.7 bWAR. Of their draft picks' total 49.1 bWAR in that span, two players account for 34.2 - Jeremy Peña and Hunter Brown. And while the Astros are bullish on recent draft classes, outside evaluations continue to rate their system among the thinnest in the sport, with top prospects mostly at the lower levels. Baseball America ranked them 25th at midseason, while MLB Pipeline and ESPN both had their system at 29th. Drafts and scouting may no longer be Flores' primary responsibility in his new role as Houston's general manager. But one of his challenges will be to replenish a poorly rated farm system while also upholding Crane's mandate that the Astros remain a perennial playoff team. What ideas or lessons from a decade overseeing scouting in St. Louis he will bring to bear on that task remains to be seen. The Flores Files Cardinals drafts under Randy Flores, with all figures courtesy of Baseball Reference: 2016 Players to reach majors: 7 Class total bWAR: 47.1 First three picks: Delvin Pérez, 23rd overall, has not played in MLB; Dylan Carlson, 33rd overall, 3.5 bWAR; Dakota Hudson, 34th overall, 3.5 bWAR Top players: Tommy Edman, sixth round, 20.7 bWAR; Zac Gallen, third round, 19.0 bWAR; Carlson and Hudson, 3.5 bWAR 2017 Players to reach majors: 5 Class total bWAR: minus-0.4 First three picks: Scott Hurst, 94th overall, 0.0 bWAR; Kramer Robertson, 124th overall, minus-0.1 bWAR; Zach Kirtley, 154th overall, has not played in MLB Top players: Kodi Whitley, 27th round, 0.3 bWAR 2018 Players to reach majors: 7 Class total bWAR: 30.2 First three picks: Nolan Gorman, 19th overall, 3.3 bWAR; Griffin Roberts, 43rd overall, has not played in MLB; Luken Baker, 75th overall, minus-0.7 bWAR Top players: Brendan Donovan, seventh round, 11.8 bWAR; Lars Nootbaar, eighth round, 10.1 bWAR; Kyle Leahy, 17th round, 3.6 bWAR 2019 Players to reach majors: 6 Class total bWAR: 7.4 First three picks: Zack Thompson, 19th overall, 0.6 bWAR; Tre Fletcher, 58th overall, has not played in MLB; Tony Locey, 96th overall, has not played in MLB Top players: Andre Pallante, fourth round, 4.3 bWAR; Pedro Pagés, sixth round, 2.6 bWAR 2020 (Draft shortened to five rounds) Players to reach majors: 3 Class total bWAR: 16.3 First three picks: Jordan Walker, 21st overall, 0.7 bWAR; Masyn Winn, 54th overall, 9.4 bWAR; Tink Hence, 63rd overall

item.title: Florida State Coaching Hot Board 1.0: Examining head coach candidates
item.description: TALLAHASSEE, FL - OCTOBER 04: Florida State Seminoles mascot Osceola and Renegade stand in the end zone before a college football game between the Miami Hurricanes and the Florida State Seminoles on October 4th, 2025 at Doak Campbell Stadium in Jacksonville, FL. (Photo by Chris Leduc/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After months (years?) of waiting, the end of the Mike Norvell era is finally here . And so, rampant speculation can finally begin to turn into some more substantive buzz surrounding who will become Florida State football’s 14th full-time head coach. We’ll get more real reporting and details over the next few days and weeks. For now, here’s our 1.0 version of the hot board of candidates to take over the Seminoles at a critical moment in the program’s history. Manny Diaz, Duke Head Coach WHY IT MAKES SENSE: He’s got real ties to the program. Diaz is an FSU grad who started his coaching career as a graduate assistant under Bobby Bowden in 1998-99 and was part of the 1999 national title staff. He’s a Miami native, which still matters for recruiting in this state, especially in South Florida. After getting fired at Miami, he went to Penn State, put together strong defenses, then took the Duke job and has actually delivered with back-to-back nine-win seasons, an outright ACC title in 2025 and a Sun Bowl win. Defensively he’s been good for a long time as a coordinator (Miami, Penn State, and earlier stops). At 52 he’s not ancient, and he’s already coached in the ACC as both a head coach and coordinator. He is one of few coaches who has rebuilt his reputation after a rough head-coaching stop, that kind of comeback story is what people love to see. Duke’s recent success under him shows he can win in the conference, and his South Florida background gives him a natural recruiting inroad that a lot of outside candidates wouldn’t have. Plus, anyone who has watched Florida State football the past season knows how bad the defense has been. Having a defensive-minded head coach could provide a big boost there. WHY IT DOESN’T MAKE SENSE: Diaz was not particularly well-liked in Miami by the end. The early energy and “The New Miami” stuff was big when he first got the job, but the results never fully matched the hype, and a lot of people in South Florida were happy to move on when Miami fired him after three seasons with a 21-15 record. That history doesn’t just disappear, and it raises the question of whether the same issues that showed up in Miami would show up again at a higher-pressure job. He also just signed an extension at Duke in April which runs through the 2031 season. Buying him out won’t be cheap — which is something FSU is probably looking for when factoring in its own buyout it is paying — and he’s in a good spot right now. Recruiting at Duke has improved, but FSU needs consistent high-level classes, not just solid ones. Whether he can scale that up, hire the right offensive staff, and handle the pressure
item.content:encoded: TALLAHASSEE, FL - OCTOBER 04: Florida State Seminoles mascot Osceola and Renegade stand in the end zone before a college football game between the Miami Hurricanes and the Florida State Seminoles on October 4th, 2025 at Doak Campbell Stadium in Jacksonville, FL. (Photo by Chris Leduc/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After months (years?) of waiting, the end of the Mike Norvell era is finally here . And so, rampant speculation can finally begin to turn into some more substantive buzz surrounding who will become Florida State football’s 14th full-time head coach. We’ll get more real reporting and details over the next few days and weeks. For now, here’s our 1.0 version of the hot board of candidates to take over the Seminoles at a critical moment in the program’s history. Manny Diaz, Duke Head Coach WHY IT MAKES SENSE: He’s got real ties to the program. Diaz is an FSU grad who started his coaching career as a graduate assistant under Bobby Bowden in 1998-99 and was part of the 1999 national title staff. He’s a Miami native, which still matters for recruiting in this state, especially in South Florida. After getting fired at Miami, he went to Penn State, put together strong defenses, then took the Duke job and has actually delivered with back-to-back nine-win seasons, an outright ACC title in 2025 and a Sun Bowl win. Defensively he’s been good for a long time as a coordinator (Miami, Penn State, and earlier stops). At 52 he’s not ancient, and he’s already coached in the ACC as both a head coach and coordinator. He is one of few coaches who has rebuilt his reputation after a rough head-coaching stop, that kind of comeback story is what people love to see. Duke’s recent success under him shows he can win in the conference, and his South Florida background gives him a natural recruiting inroad that a lot of outside candidates wouldn’t have. Plus, anyone who has watched Florida State football the past season knows how bad the defense has been. Having a defensive-minded head coach could provide a big boost there. WHY IT DOESN’T MAKE SENSE: Diaz was not particularly well-liked in Miami by the end. The early energy and “The New Miami” stuff was big when he first got the job, but the results never fully matched the hype, and a lot of people in South Florida were happy to move on when Miami fired him after three seasons with a 21-15 record. That history doesn’t just disappear, and it raises the question of whether the same issues that showed up in Miami would show up again at a higher-pressure job. He also just signed an extension at Duke in April which runs through the 2031 season. Buying him out won’t be cheap — which is something FSU is probably looking for when factoring in its own buyout it is paying — and he’s in a good spot right now. Recruiting at Duke has improved, but FSU needs consistent high-level classes, not just solid ones. Whether he can scale that up, hire the right offensive staff, and handle the pressure and expectations that come with this job is still an open question. Rising stock is nice, but it also means other schools could be interested, and after finding something that works at Duke he might not be in a rush to leave a stable situation for a rebuild. The last time he was a head coach at a Florida school the results were uneven, and the game has only gotten harder since then. -Tony Morris Glenn Schumann, Georgia Defensive Coordinator WHY IT MAKES SENSE: Could Schumann be the next Kirby Smart? Smart spent nine seasons working under Nick Saban and as his star rose, it became clear that Smart only had eyes for the Georgia job. Once it opened, he finally made the move, bringing Schumann (who was the director of football operations for Bama after spending time as a grad assistant) along with him as the first coach he hired. Schumann is now in his 11th season at Georgia, having worked his way up from inside linebackers coach to co-defensive coordinator (alongside Dan Lanning and later Will Muschamp) and finally to the sole DC role in 2024. Could his eyes be set on a job like Florida State? The timing could be perfect to make the move. Schumann has been part of six national championship teams at Alabama and Georgia, and his time under Nick Saban and Smart has primed him for a head coaching job. He wouldn’t command a major salary but wouldn’t come cheap, either. Under Schumann’s guidance as the sole defensive coordinator, Georgia’s defense ranked 10th in the nation in 2025 and 23rd nationally in 2024. In 2023, Georgia ranked fifth nationally in scoring defense (15.6 points per game) and topped the country in third-down-conversion defense (25.7%). From 2019-2022, Georgia led the nation in combined scoring defense (13.6 points per game) and rushing defense (75.7 yards per game) while ranking second in total defense. Schumann has been an integral part of that success, and we haven’t even touched on his recruiting chops yet. Schumann is an elite recruiter, plain and simple. He’s played a significant role in landing 13 five-star recruits and dozens of four-star prospects, the vast majority of whom were victories over other top programs in the nation. He’s beaten FSU head to head for players such as Nakobe Dean, Raylen Wilson, Daylen Everette and Channing Tindall, and he knows the recruiting rigors in states like Georgia and Florida like the back of his hand. How about as a developer? Since becoming Georgia’s inside linebackers position coach in 2016, he’s produced an incredible three Butkus Award winners (given to the nation’s best linebacker): Roquan Smith (2017), Nakobe Dean (2021), and Jalon Walker (2024). WHY IT DOESN’T MAKE SENSE: All of the accolades above look great, right? But then … why is he still at Georgia? Smart and Schumann are intertwined a great deal and many folks (myself included) think Smart deserves the lion’s share of credit for Georgia’s outstanding defenses in the early 2020s. It’s always a major gamble when you hire a coordinator working under a head coach who specializes on the same side of the ball. College football history is littered with coordinators who left the shadows of their bosses for head coaching positions, only to return to the shadows a few seasons later because they couldn’t hack it in the head coach’s seat. If indeed the Georgia defenses were primary products of Smart (and Lanning as co-DC), would Schumann be able to replicate those heights on his own? Schumann is only 36 years old, so what kind of staff would he be able to assemble? Moving from a situation like Georgia to a situation like FSU may not be appealing for more established assistant coaches and Schumann isn’t exactly well-traveled enough to have a big book of potential staff hires. Another interesting caveat is how Georgia fans currently feel about Schumann. Suffice it to say, he isn’t too popular in Athens. Every program’s fanbase chooses a scapegoat on the assistant coaching staff when things aren’t going right. Schumann seems to be that guy for Dawg faithful. Have things just gotten stale? Has he become complacent? Eleven seasons coaching the same unit is an eternity in contemporary college football landscape. Would a change of scenery help, or would it be a harbinger of things to come under a first-time head coach? -NoleThruandThru Jimbo Fisher, ACCN analyst WHY IT MAKES SENSE: For at least a portion of the FSU fanbase, Fisher is the clear favorite for the job now that Norvell is gone. It’s not entirely surprising. He’s the last guy to win a national title in Tallahassee, went 83-23, won three straight ACC titles, the 2013 national championship and led the Seminoles to a 29-game winning streak. Those years were when FSU was a blue-blood and a real powerhouse year after year had older fans reminiscing to the Bobby Bowden era. A lot of people who checked out over the last few seasons could come back for that version of the program. He also recruited at a level FSU hasn’t touched since he l

item.title: When will the Golden State Valkyries parade be? Here's what to know
item.description: After Golden State Valkyries achieved an historic win, beating the Atlanta Dream, 68-63, Saturday night at Ballhalla, the team announced details of their championship parade! The Valkyries and the City of San Francisco will host the parade along the city's Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Here's what you need to know. What time will the parade start? Fans can begin lining up along the parade route at 9 a.m. on the bay side of the Embarcadero. The parade will start at noon and expected to end at 2 p.m. Where will the parade be? The parade will start at noon at the Ferry Building, travel along the Embarcadero, and end at King and 2nd streets. If I can't watch in person, how else can I watch? Viewers can watch coverage on TV on ABC7, or stream on the free ABC7 Bay Area streaming and mobile app starting at 9:30 a.m. on Wednesday. Who will be there? The team, coaches, staff and city leaders will all be there to celebrate the historic win. According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade. Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said. RELATED: Golden State Valkyries win its 1st WNBA title, beating Atlanta Dream, 68-63 Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night. Are there fan opportunities? Yes! Fan opportunities will include a viewing area, a championship merchandise truck, and various fan activation zones along the parade route. How will the weather be on Wednesday? < /strong> It will be partly cloudy along the bay with temperatures in the upper 60s. Street Closures and Public Transportation Fans and workers in the area are encouraged to take public transportation such as BART and Muni due to some street closures. Street Closures The following streets will be closed from 12:01 a.m. to 4:00 PM on November 4 -Eastbound King Street and Northbound Embarcadero between Third Street (at King Street) and Broadway (at Embarcadero) -Market Street between Drumm Street and Steuart Street -Steuart Street between Market Street and southerly terminus -Spear Street between Market Street and southerly terminus The following streets will be closed from 8:00 a.m. to 4 p.m. on November 4 -Southbound Embarcadero and Westbound King between Broadway (at Embarcadero) and Third Street (at King Street) -Washington Street between Drumm Street and the Embarcadero -Mission, Howard, Folsom, Harrison and Bryant streets between Main Street and the Embarcadero -Brannan Street between Second Street and the Embarcadero, with local access maintained to Delancey Street -Townsend Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero -Second Street between Brannan Street and King Street BART and Muni Met

According to the Golden State Valkyries, Oakland Mayor Barbara Lee, San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie, San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan, and city officials from across the Bay, are expected to be at the championship parade. Gabby Williams, who was named WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, will bang the GSV drum alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie to start the parade, the team said. RELATED: Golden State Valkyries win its 1st WNBA title, beating Atlanta Dream, 68-63 Golden State Valkyries captured a championship in just their second season by beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a sensational first WNBA Finals Game 7 on Saturday night. Are there fan opportunities? Yes! Fan opportunities will include a viewing area, a championship merchandise truck, and various fan activation zones along the parade route. How will the weather be on Wednesday? < /strong> It will be partly cloudy along the bay with temperatures in the upper 60s. Street Closures and Public Transportation Fans and workers in the area are encouraged to take public transportation such as BART and Muni due to some street closures. Street Closures The following streets will be closed from 12:01 a.m. to 4:00 PM on November 4 -Eastbound King Street and Northbound Embarcadero between Third Street (at King Street) and Broadway (at Embarcadero) -Market Street between Drumm Street and Steuart Street -Steuart Street between Market Street and southerly terminus -Spear Street between Market Street and southerly terminus The following streets will be closed from 8:00 a.m. to 4 p.m. on November 4 -Southbound Embarcadero and Westbound King between Broadway (at Embarcadero) and Third Street (at King Street) -Washington Street between Drumm Street and the Embarcadero -Mission, Howard, Folsom, Harrison and Bryant streets between Main Street and the Embarcadero -Brannan Street between Second Street and the Embarcadero, with local access maintained to Delancey Street -Townsend Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero -Second Street between Brannan Street and King Street BART and Muni Metro riders can exit at Embarcadero or Montgomery stations and walk to the parade route. BART will run additional trains and increase staffing and security to accommodate parade-day crowds. For the latest service information and travel updates, visit bart.gov/valkyries . Muni Service Adjustments Muni service on the F and N lines along the Embarcadero will be suspended from approximately 9:30 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. Alternate service for Muni streetcars along the Embarcadero will be provided by the 15 Bayview Hunters Point Express bus that will be rerouted onto 2nd Street and pick up at the following locations: Northbound Fourth Street and Townsend Street Third Street between Townsend Street and Brannan Street Second Street between Brannan Street and Bryant Street Second Street and Harrison Street Second Street and Howard Street Second Street and Market Street Southbound Second Street between Market Street and Mission Street Second Street and Howard Street Harrison Street and Second Street Fourth Street and Townsend Street Muni ambassadors will be on site at affected stops to direct passengers to alternative locations. For all transit and traffic updates, please visit www.sfmta.com/valkyries. Autonomous Vehicles City partners have worked in close coordination with autonomous vehicle operators to reduce congestion in dense, high-foot traffic zones around the parade route. Autonomous vehicle operations will be restricted in the following areas from 12:01 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. on November 4: -On the Embarcadero, south of Battery Street -In the Financial District, streets south of Washington Street and east of Battery Street -In the South of Market, streets east of First Street InSouth Beach : -Bryant Street between Second Street and the Embarcadero -Brannan Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero -Townsend Street between Third Street and the Embarcadero -King Street between Fifth Street and the Embarcadero -Berry Street between Fifth Street and Third Street -Second Street between Bryant Street and King Street -Third Street between Brannan Street and Mission Creek Channel -Fourth Street between Townsend Street and Mission Creek Channel -Autonomous vehicle riders will see available pickup and drop-off locations in their respective phone apps. Pick-up and drop-off will be restricted on the following streets: -Battery Street between the Embarcadero and Market Street -First Street between Market Street and Harrison Street -Third Street between Folsom Street and Brannan Street -Fourth Street between Harrison Street and Townsend Street San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office contributed to this report For more information from the Mayor Lurie's office, click here . item.title: Falcons – Buccaneers instant recap: The rain washes away any shine from our favorite team
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We hoped and prayed the Falcons would buck a seemingly ancient trend of falling down after a major win against a contender, and we hoped and prayed in vain. Our favorite team went to Tampa Bay in a downpour that turned into a drizzle and washed away their hopes of taking possession of the NFC South lead with an embarrassing effort that undermined almost every positive the Falcons have put forth in recent weeks. Let’s be honest about what we saw Sunday: It was an ass kicking where Atlanta was entirely out-coached, out-played, and out-hustled. Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass, yet the Buccaneers didn’t care because they ran for 300 yards. The Falcons had Bijan Robinson, but somehow that didn’t matter because the Falcons got down after throwing too much and then started throwing nonstop late. The Falcons were within striking distance—or at least not dead—all day, but yet could not turn in a single point. There is nothing that can be said about the caliber of performance the Falcons put on the field today that is positive, and aside from a handful of strong individual performances, Atlanta was humiliated and humbled by their rival. Now 3-5, the Falcons are back down with the Buccaneers and the division is a muddle, and Atlanta’s highs are matched by their lows as they continue to be defined by inconsistency and utterly baffling performances after stunningly good ones. This loss is impossible to justify and tough to swallow, and this is the kind of doubt-sprouting performance that the Falcons will now be combating the rest of the year. item.content:encoded: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers runs against the Atlanta Falcons during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images We hoped and prayed the Falcons would buck a seemingly ancient trend of falling down after a major win against a contender, and we hoped and prayed in vain. Our favorite team went to Tampa Bay in a downpour that turned into a drizzle and washed away their hopes of taking possession of the NFC South lead with an embarrassing effort that undermined almost every positive the Falcons have put forth in recent weeks. Let’s be honest about what we saw Sunday: It was an ass kicking where Atlanta was entirely out-coached, out-played, and out-hustled. Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass, yet the Buccaneers didn’t care because they ran for 300 yards. The Falcons had Bijan Robinson, but somehow that didn’t matter because the Falcons got down after throwing too much and then started throwing nonstop late. The Falcons were within striking distance—or at least not dead—all day, but yet could not turn in a single point. Now 3-5, the Falcons are back down with the Buccaneers and the division is a muddle, and Atlanta’s highs are matched by their lows as they continue to be defined by inconsistency and utterly baffling performances after stunningly good ones. This loss is impossible to justify and tough to swallow, and this is the kind of doubt-sprouting performance that the Falcons will now be combating the rest of the year. Here’s a drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. I suggest not bothering to read it, but thanks for stopping by. 1st Quarter Bijan picked up three yards on first down, then Michael Penix Jr. hit Jahan Dotson for 19 yards. Bijan picked up three and then Penix hit Kyle Pitts for five yards, and then Bijan got a yard. Penix went up the gut on fourth down to convert. Bijan then went two yards and then was stalled for no gain, and Penix couldn’t connect with Drake London. In the rain from 53 yards, Nick Folk’s field goal attempt went wide left. The Buccaneers took over near midfield, and then Bucky Irving took it almost 20 yards. Irving got a yard on first down. After three yards, Kendal Daniels got Irving out of bounds. Baker Mayfield then bombed it downfield and threw it a bit behind his receiver, who had it knocked loose by Mike Hughes, who arrived with excellent timing. Chase McLaughlin’s field goal try was good to make it 3-0 Buccaneers. Zachariah Branch took it to about the 28, and an illegal formation call on the Buccaneers gave Atlanta five more yards. On the next play, Penix simply missed the defender and threw an interception right to him, with Drake London picking up a 15 yard penalty for unnecessary roughness on the same play. Buccaneers ball. Irving took it five yards on first down. Then in a wildly bewildering sequence, Baker Mayfield got out of a busted situation, scrambled, flipped the ball to Bucky Irving, and Irving was galloping toward the end zone…only to have Jessie Bates come in and chop the ball out of his hands, where it landed out of bounds in the end zone. Falcons ball! Bijan Robinson got called for a first down, and then picked up five yards. Penix didn’t see anything downfield on second down, and tried the outlet to Bijan, who dropped it. Then Penix threw another interception, again to Anzalone. Buccaneers ball. Irving was stopped for a loss by Brandon Dorlus. Irving then got three yards. Mayfield missed badly on third down, setting up a McLaughlin field goal. 6-0 Buccaneers. Branch slid down past the 25 yard line. Bijan then took it for four yards. Bijan then cut it inside for another four. Penix evaded the pressure, but wildly overthrew Pitts. The Jake Bailey punt rolled to the 13 yard line. Bucky Irving then picked up 12 yards on first down. Baker fumbled the snap and handed it to Irving, who got a yard. Irving then got a couple more yards on second down. Gainwell was then quickly tackled after maybe a yard. 2nd Quarter Dotson called for a fair catch on the Falcons 39 yard line. Bijan then appeared to run into the pile for a minimal gain, but emerged on the other side for almost 15 yards. Then he picked up two yards. Penix then made a dangerous arcing throw to Dotson, who had it bounce off his hands. Khalil Herbert then ran into the pile for maybe a yard. The Falcons then went for it on fourth down, and Penix threw an interception again. Bucs ball. Irving spun his way to five yards, and then Mayfield scrambled for a first down. Irving then picked up another five yards. Irivng was tripped up by Daniels for another four yards. Irving got another first down and five yards, and followed that up with six yards. Irving was then tackled by Zach Harrison on second down just shy of a first down. Maason Smith then got Gainwell, but not before he squeezed past the line for another first down. Gainwell then took it almost 20 yards. Gainwell went up the middle for a yard or two. A false start on the Bucs backed them up five yards. Mayfield had the ball flip out of his hand and then ran for five yards. A carry for Gainwell then went for three yards, setting up a field goal try. McLaughlin hit it again to make it 9-0 Buccaneers. A one yard gain by Bijan gave way to a nice, physical run where he picked up nine yards and a first down. Herbert then picked up two yards. Penix then sort of threw it away to the sideline in the direction of a receiver. Bijan somehow then managed to bully his way to a first down on 3rd and 8, but on booth review he was ruled down after a six yard gain. On fourth down, they gave it to Bijan, who came up a little short of a conversion. Bucs ball. Irving then rolled for 13 yards on first down. C.J. Henderson then got Irving after a couple of yards. Irving then got two more, and Stefanski surprisingly called a timeout. Gainwell was hit by Cameron Thomas and got a yard, with Atlanta spending their last timeout. Ryan Neuzil’s snap bounced off Matthew Bergeron’s leg. Half over. 3rd Quarter The Bucs returned it to about the 28 yard line, and then Irving went two yards. Irving then picked up three yards. Baker Mayfield’s pass to Gainwell was tipped and ultimately dropped by the running back. Punt, and it went over Jahan Dotson’s head and rolled back inside the 10 yard line. Bijan was stonewalled on first down. Bijan then took it about seven yards. Pitts then caught a short pass and took it just shy of a first down. Punt. Mayfield faked a pass and scrambled for three yards. Irving then ran into a brick wall. Mayfield tried to scramble and was brought down for a loss. The Falcons get the ball back after a penalty and a touchback. Bijan rolled forward for a yard, and then picked up another yard on second down. A quick pass to Herbert went for five yards. Punt, and Mike Ford Jr. got Tez Johnson inside the 10 yard line. Irving took it eight yards on first down. Irving then got loose and ran to the Falcons 35 for 46 yards. Kenneth Gainwell then went one yard. Gainwell then got loose, evading multiple tackle attempts and picking up 28 yards. Irving was smothered after maybe a yard. Irving then powered through contact to pick up a touchdown. 16-0 Buccaneers. Herbert took it to about the 35 yard line on the kickoff return. Penix then felt pressure and threw it at Herbert’s feet, but a roughing the passer call gave the Falcons life. Herbert then took it almost nine yards. Herbert then got tackled for no gain, with one defender latching on to his ankles. Bijan was then stuffed. On fourth down, Penix scrambled for a first down. Austin Hooper then made a leaping roll on a catch for nine yards. Penix then had to throw

item.title: 'They don't know the rules!' – Jose Mourinho mocks Racing Santander fans after Real Madrid's 3-0 win
item.description: Real Racing Club de Santander v Real Madrid - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho was back to his provocative best following Real Madrid's clinical 3-0 victory over Racing Santander on Sunday afternoon. Despite a hostile atmosphere, the Portuguese tactician took the opportunity to mock the home supporters for their lack of understanding regarding the laws of the game. Mourinho targets 'ignorant' home support Real Madrid secured a vital three points on their travels , but the post-match headlines were dominated by Mourinho's characteristic wit. The former Chelsea and Inter boss was far from intimidated by the atmosphere at the Estadio El Sardinero, choosing instead to dismantle the home crowd's vocal protests during his post-match press conference. 'I love this stadium and I love the Racing fans. They don't come to attend a show or watch a movie, they come to participate in the match and make things very difficult for the opponents,' Mourinho explained. However, the mood shifted as he addressed the constant whistling from the stands. 'They protested against every decision of the referee, especially because they did not know the rules well. And of course, I understand, because the rules change so much,' he added with a heavy dose of irony. The tension in the stadium peaked when Racing Santander thought they had earned a way back into the game via the penalty spot. However, a VAR intervention eventually led to the decision being overturned, a move that sparked fury among the local supporters. VAR controversy and officiating praise Mourinho's comments focused heavily on the cancelled penalty, which he believed was a clear-cut example of the technology working exactly as intended. The Portuguese manager stood firm in his belief that the home side were never entitled to a spot-kick under the current guidelines. 'They protested against this cancelled penalty, when it was obvious that the rule says that it is never a penalty. It was very obvious, as long as the VAR was not sleeping. And the VAR was awake, fortunately. The referee was very good,' Mourinho continued. Clinical Madrid keep pace at the top On the pitch, the narrative was far more straightforward as Real Madrid's star power eventually overwhelmed the hosts. Kylian Mbappe continued his extraordinary record in Spanish football by maintaining a perfect scoring record against every opponent he has encountered in La Liga, while Jude Bellingham - who became the first English player in history to score 50 goals for the club - and Yan Diomande added further gloss to the scoreline. The result was crucial for Real Madrid to keep the pressure firmly on their title rivals, as they now sit third in the La Liga standings with 27 points - just a single point behind second-placed Atletico Madrid and trailing leaders Barcelona by three points. item.title: Watch Burna Boy Take Over the NFL Paris Game with a Star-Studded Halftime Show
item.description: Burna Boy backstage at Stade de France wearing a custom 3.PARADIS leather jacket look for the NFL Paris Game. Did you catch Burna Boy at the inaugural NFL Paris Game last weekend? If you missed his halftime performance at the Stade de France in Paris, we have all the details. The Nigerian Grammy Award winner took over the pitch as the Pittsburgh Steelers faced the New Orleans Saints, giving American football fans a taste of West African music. Returning to the 80,000-capacity stadium after his historic solo concert in Paris, Burna Boy opened his set with “ 4 Kampe II ”, his collaboration with French-Haitian singer Joé Dwèt Filé . He moved between English, French and Haitian Creole before welcoming French singer Yseult on stage and moving into some of his biggest hits. The set included “ On the Low ,” “ Ye ” and “ Last Last ,” with a special appearance from French judo champion Teddy Riner adding to the occasion. It was a set that gave fans in the stadium and viewers watching around the world a taste of the Nigerian star’s catalogue. Burna Boy arrives at Stade de France ahead of his halftime show performance at the NFL Paris Game in Paris. Burna Boy also made sure his outfit matched the scale of the performance. He wore custom luxury streetwear, pairing a structured oversized leather jacket with tailored cargo trousers, heavy silver neck chains and dark tinted sunglasses. The NFL Paris Game adds to Burna Boy’s growing list of major international sporting appearances. He has previously performed at the NBA All-Star Game and the UEFA Champions League Final kickoff show, taking African music to audiences well beyond the usual concert stage. The Paris weekend also coincided with the launch of his debut sneaker collaboration with Swiss sportswear brand On, under the No Giant Stands Alone campaign. Away from the stage, he was also spotted backstage catching up with French football star Paul Pogba . Watch below *** Photo Credit: Burna Boy/Instagram The post Watch Burna Boy Take Over the NFL Paris Game with a Star-Studded Halftime Show appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

Morocco, which claims the region as its own, welcomed the decision, while its opponents from the Algeria-backed Polisario Front called it "unacceptable".

item.title: Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list
item.description: …Bishop Obodo demands removal of his name, warns of legal action By Anayo Okoli The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has disowned the inclusion of the Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu, Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, in the Enugu State All Progressives Congress, APC, Campaign Council, saying he was listed without his knowledge or consent. The Diocese also demanded the immediate removal of the bishop’s name and those of other Catholic priests allegedly included in the campaign council without their authorisation. Obodo, who is also the Enugu State Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, was reportedly named Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the APC campaign council. In a disclaimer dated October 30, 2026, and signed by the Diocesan Chancellor and Secretary, Very Rev. Fr. Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition. The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation. “The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests. “We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said. The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties. It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good. While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests. “We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said. The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added. The post Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list appeared first on Vanguard News .

Wilfred Chidi Agubuchie, the Diocese described the inclusion as unauthorised, misleading and a misrepresentation of the bishop’s political disposition. The statement said the action was a “malicious act of misrepresentation and defamation,” adding that it undermined the bishop’s integrity and ecclesiastical reputation. “The Catholic Diocese of Enugu has become aware of reports concerning the inclusion of the name of Most Rev. Ernest Anezichukwu Obodo, Auxiliary Bishop of Enugu and Chairman of the Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), Enugu State, as Director of the Faith-Based Campaign Group in the Enugu State APC Campaign Council, alongside the names of some Catholic priests. “We categorically state that the inclusion of the Bishop’s name without his knowledge or consent is wholly unauthorised, misleading and unacceptable,” the statement said. The Diocese stressed that the Catholic Church did not engage in partisan politics, participate in political campaigns or endorse political parties. It said the Church remained politically neutral and committed to its spiritual mission and the promotion of peace, justice and the common good. While acknowledging the right of individual Christians to participate in civic and democratic activities, the Diocese warned against using the name, office or identity of the Church and its ministers for partisan political interests. “We therefore demand the immediate removal of Bishop Ernest Obodo’s name, as well as the names of all other Catholic priests included without their knowledge and consent, from the said campaign list and any related publications,” it said. The Diocese further warned that any continued or subsequent unauthorised use of the bishop’s name, title, image or ecclesiastical office for partisan political purposes would attract appropriate legal action. “For the avoidance of doubt, the Catholic Church is not a political campaign organisation and must not be presented as one,” the statement added. The post Catholic Diocese disowns Enugu APC campaign council list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Stop opposition politics, integrate with FG, Soludo tells South-East leaders
item.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged South-East political leaders to abandon opposition politics and embrace greater integration with the Federal Government. Soludo made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting on Sunday in Awka. The meeting had political leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and Accord Party. The governor said that the coalition of political parties in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election represented a new direction for the region’s political engagement. According to him, the era of opposition politics, which became prominent in the South-East during the 2015 general elections, should give way to active participation in governance at the centre. He said that considerable work was required at the grassroots to change public perception of the government and mobilise support for the president. He argued that the 5,000 votes Tinubu received in Anambra in the 2023 presidential election had contributed to attracting significant projects to the state and the region. “If 5,000 votes could attract these projects to our state and the region, imagine what would happen if we mobilised the electorate to give him massive support,” he said. On the economic reforms of the government, Soludo acknowledged efforts to stabilise foreign exchange availability and address fiscal challenges, noting that, although progress had been made, more work was required. He called for structural realignment of the coalition, saying existing campaign and mobilisation structures would be streamlined during the week. The governor urged grassroots mobilisers to adopt door-to-door campaigns, drawing lessons from successful political mobilisation strategies used during the 1983 elections. He also advised campaign teams not to be distracted by opposition criticism and verbal attacks on social media, but to remain focused on communicating what he described as the truth. Soludo reaffirmed his commitment to long-term governance, saying that the decisions being taken by his administration were aimed at securing a prosperous future for generations to come. Earlier, APGA National Chairman, Mr Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as a landmark in the political history of Anambra. Ezeokenwa said that the coalition was an unprecedented political alignment involving different parties united in support of Tinubu’s re-election. He commended Soludo for providing leadership and facilitating the alliance, assuring that APGA would fully support the governor’s political direction. “Our party structure is ready to execute the instructions and deliver results at the polls,” he said. Also speaking, APC Chairman in Anambra, Sen. Emma Anosike, expressed appreciation for the development strides in the state. item.title: 2027: Otti warns supporters against disrupting opposition campaigns
item.description: Threatens arrest for anyone obstructing rival parties By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has warned Labour Party supporters against disrupting the campaign activities of opposition parties ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that he has not authorised anyone to interfere with their democratic rights. Otti said anyone found obstructing rival political parties from holding lawful rallies or other campaign activities would face arrest, irrespective of party affiliation. The governor gave the warning on Sunday in Umuahia while flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he stressed that political competition must be conducted within the confines of the law. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said. Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed. He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadia, provided they followed the necessary procedures, obtained relevant approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Otti added that he had directed security agencies to ensure that no political group was prevented from carrying out legitimate campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” he said. Addressing party loyalists, the governor warned that membership of the ruling party would not confer immunity on anyone who attempted to undermine the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond campaign conduct, Otti challenged opposition parties to focus their campaigns on policy alternatives and the future development of the state rather than personal attacks or issues he said his administration had addressed. He argued that political debate in Abia should move beyond the payment of salaries and pensions, road construction and environmental sanitation to broader development priorities. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. He urged opposition parties to examine available performance data before making claims about the state, citing its ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations. “You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said. The governor also cited feedback from Abians at home and abroad, as well as development opportunities offered by multilateral institutions, as indications of progress under his administration. “It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he said. Otti thanked residents for attending the campaign flag-off and urged Labour Party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation across the state. “This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added. The event featured the presentation of party flags to Labour Party candidates for the 2027 National and State Houses of Assembly elections. Party members, candidates and supporters attended the ceremony, chanting solidarity songs in support of their respective candidates. item.title: NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal
item.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — A chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Barrister Peter Agubuzu, has faulted the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, over his criticism of a proposal for the South-East to accept a single four-year presidential term. Agubuzu described Kalu’s remarks as misplaced, urging him to focus on addressing the economic hardship and rising cost of living confronting Nigerians rather than dwelling on how long the South-East might wait to produce a President. Kalu had reportedly criticised South-East stakeholders advocating a single four-year presidential term for the region, an arrangement attributed to the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Speaking at an All Progressives Congress (APC) women’s rally in Enugu on Saturday, the Deputy Speaker reportedly said the Igbo could not afford to wait 60 years to produce a President who would serve for only four years. Reacting, Agubuzu, a senior lawyer, said the immediate concern of Nigerians was the worsening economic situation and the need for leadership capable of addressing the country’s challenges. He argued that Obi’s proposal was driven by the need to transform Nigeria’s economy from consumption to production and lift millions of citizens out of poverty. “While Nigerians across the country are chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ because of the economic hardship they are experiencing and their fear of a worsening economic crisis if Tinubu is re-elected, our brother, the Deputy Speaker, is talking about 60 years. “He forgot that Obi’s primary objective is to transform Nigeria from consumption to production to lift millions out of poverty. This is why Nigerians are chanting Tinubu Must Go,” Agubuzu said. He maintained that the major concern of Obi was how to address the country’s economic difficulties and restore hope to millions of Nigerians struggling with the rising cost of living. “What Nigerians are saying is straightforward: Peter Obi should come and salvage the country from the impending economic disaster they fear will follow if President Tinubu is re-elected. “Nigerians are worried about their survival, their livelihoods and the future of their children. That is the urgent issue before us, not a speculative debate about waiting 60 years for an Igbo President,” he said. The NDC chieftain further argued that discussions about a single presidential term should be considered within the broader context of national unity, equity and political inclusion. He urged political leaders to pay greater attention to the concerns of ordinary Nigerians and focus on practical solutions to the country’s economic challenges rather than allow debates over regional claims to the presidency to overshadow demands for effective leadership. The post NDC chieftain tackles Kalu over Obi’s four-year presidency proposal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Akpabio predicts highest South-South votes for Tinubu from Akwa Ibom
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, has expressed confidence that Akwa Ibom State will deliver the highest number of votes for President Bola Tinubu in the South-South region in the 2027 presidential election. Akpabio made the declaration on Sunday during a special church service at the International Christian Worship Centre, Uyo, organised to dedicate the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 election campaigns to God. The service had the theme, “We Are Well Able”. In a statement by his Special Assistant on Media, Jackson Udom, the Senate President said Akwa Ibom indigenes, particularly APC members, must close ranks and present a united front to ensure the party’s success at the polls. He said the state had a responsibility to reciprocate the support President Tinubu had given him by mobilising votes for the President. According to him, the support of Tinubu contributed to his emergence as Senate President, making him the number three citizen in the country. “Whether you like him or not, he is there today. The only way to thank Mr President for that support is to give him all our votes. “From what I have seen here today, Akwa Ibom State will give Mr President the highest number of votes in the South-South region,” he said. In an address titled, “One Family, One Destiny, One Akwa Ibom Under God”, Akpabio said while the people acknowledged God’s sovereignty over their individual and collective destinies, they must also uphold righteousness, justice and mercy. He described Akwa Ibom as a Nigerian success story, attributing its progress to purposeful leadership, peace and development. The Senate President said development should not be measured only by roads and buildings but also by the bridges built between people and the hope restored in their lives. He urged political leaders and party members to sustain the state’s progress and ensure that its future achievements surpassed those already recorded. On party unity, Akpabio cautioned against divisions between old and new members of the APC, insisting that all members should be treated equally. “In the APC family, there should be no aborigines and no newcomers; no landlords and no tenants; no first-class members and no second-class members. There should be only one big family, united by a common purpose and a shared responsibility,” he said. Using a biblical reference from John 14:2, he said there was room for everyone in the party, regardless of when they joined or their political standing. He added that political ambitions should not override the welfare of the people, urging party members to conduct their campaigns in ways that respect human dignity. Akpabio further said the development of Akwa Ibom was inseparable from the progress of Nigeria, stressing that the state could not remain indifferent to insecurity and hardship in other parts of the country. “Nigeria is not merely the nation to which Akwa Ibom belongs; it is the larger destiny to which Akwa Ibom c

item.title: Anambra coalition is battle for Nigeria’s soul – Soludo
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the political coalition formed by parties in the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a battle for the soul of Nigeria and Ndigbo. Soludo, who is the Anambra State Coordinator of Tinubu’s re-election campaign, spoke on Sunday during the inauguration of the presidential campaign structure at the International Convention Centre, Awka. He said the coalition, which brings together political leaders across party lines, was formed primarily to secure Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that Ndigbo must actively participate in national politics rather than remain on the sidelines. The governor described the forthcoming political contest as a clash between emotion and reason, expressing the view that emotional politics could only dominate temporarily before giving way to strategic calculations. Addressing candidates contesting other elective positions on different party platforms, Soludo assured them of a level playing field, but stressed that the coalition’s common objective was to ensure Tinubu’s return to office. He recalled that prominent Igbo political leaders, including Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, Dr. Alex Ekwueme and Dr. Chuba Okadigbo, played significant roles in national politics, insisting that the South-East could not afford to isolate itself from developments at the centre. According to him, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, recognised the importance of national political engagement and consequently resolved to align with the Federal Government. He said APGA and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, shared progressive ideals anchored on federalism and shared prosperity, adding that Tinubu understood the need for progressives to work together for national development. Reflecting on his political journey, which he said began in 1980 under the principle of “one nation, one destiny”, Soludo urged Ndigbo to consider their long-term political and economic interests. He argued that state revenues alone could not adequately finance major infrastructure such as federal rail lines and gas pipelines without strategic partnerships with the Federal Government. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has described the political coalition formed by parties in the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid as a battle for the soul of Nigeria and Ndigbo. Soludo, who is the Anambra State Coordinator of Tinubu’s re-election campaign, spoke on Sunday during the inauguration of the presidential campaign structure at the International Convention Centre, Awka. He said the coalition, which brings together political leaders across party lines, was formed primarily to secure Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that Ndigbo must actively participate in national politics rather than remain on the sidelines. The governor described the forthcoming political contest as a clash between emotion and reason, expressing the view that emotional politics could only dominate temporarily before giving way to strategic calculations. Addressing candidates contesting other elective positions on different party platforms, Soludo assured them of a level playing field, but stressed that the coalition’s common objective was to ensure Tinubu’s return to office. He recalled that prominent Igbo political leaders, including Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, Dr. Alex Ekwueme and Dr. Chuba Okadigbo, played significant roles in national politics, insisting that the South-East could not afford to isolate itself from developments at the centre. According to him, the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, recognised the importance of national political engagement and consequently resolved to align with the Federal Government. He said APGA and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, shared progressive ideals anchored on federalism and shared prosperity, adding that Tinubu understood the need for progressives to work together for national development. Reflecting on his political journey, which he said began in 1980 under the principle of “one nation, one destiny”, Soludo urged Ndigbo to consider their long-term political and economic interests. He argued that state revenues alone could not adequately finance major infrastructure such as federal rail lines and gas pipelines without strategic partnerships with the Federal Government. The governor also noted that despite Tinubu securing about 5,000 votes in Anambra State during the 2023 presidential election, his administration had extended support to the state. He expressed optimism that greater federal interventions could come if more people in Anambra supported the President in the next election. Soludo called for an end to what he described as opposition and protest politics practised in the state since 2015, urging Ndigbo to embrace active participation in governance at the national level. He further argued that a fragmented opposition would find it difficult to defeat an incumbent president, adding that his assessment was informed by his claimed record of correctly predicting presidential election outcomes in Nigeria since 1983. On the future of presidential power rotation, Soludo said that following the completion of the South’s second term, power was expected to return to the North before rotating back to the South around 2039. He urged Ndigbo to position themselves within the national political structure ahead of that period. On political differences within Anambra, the governor said he maintained cordial personal and family relationships with political opponents, stressing that their disagreements were limited to political strategies and ideologies. He also acknowledged federal fiscal interventions aimed at improving foreign exchange availability for importers, noting that although progress had been made, more work remained. Outlining the campaign’s next steps, Soludo said political structures across the state would be streamlined before the end of the following week. He maintained that elections were won at polling units and ward levels, urging supporters to remain focused despite criticism and verbal attacks on social media. In his remarks, the APC state chairman, Senator Emma Anosike, said he had initially been sceptical about the meeting but expressed appreciation for what he described as the developmental strides recorded in Anambra. Anosike said the coalition was intended to ensure the state’s direct participation in national governance. He called for unity among party members, while noting that candidates contesting on different platforms were free to demonstrate their individual political strengths. He, however, urged all stakeholders to work together towards Tinubu’s re-election. Also speaking, the APGA National Chairman, Barrister Sly Ezeokenwa, described the gathering as an unprecedented coalition united by the objective of securing Tinubu’s re-election. He commended Soludo for facilitating the political alignment and pledged the readiness of APGA’s structures to implement campaign directives and mobilise support for the President. The event attracted representatives of several political parties, including the PDP, Accord Party, APGA and APC, in what organisers described as a broad-based political alliance ahead of the 2027 presidential election. item.title: “He could no longer deliver” – Ten Hag explains why Ronaldo struggled at Man United
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has criticised Cristiano Ronaldo’s fitness and commitment during their time together at Old Trafford, saying the Portuguese forward could “no longer deliver” at the highest level after leaving Juventus in 2021. Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch club FC Twente, made the remarks during an interview with ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie on Sunday, reflecting on his strained relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner. Ronaldo returned to Manchester United from Juventus in 2021 and scored 27 goals in 54 appearances under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ten Hag. However, his relationship with the Dutch manager deteriorated as he was frequently left out of the starting line-up. United eventually terminated his contract in November 2022 following his explosive interview with Piers Morgan, in which he said he felt “betrayed” by Ten Hag and criticised the club’s hierarchy. Reflecting on the challenges of managing the forward, Ten Hag said Ronaldo’s reluctance to put the team first created problems within the squad. “The challenge is to get the team functioning, really as always. Every player is important in that and you need top players to be able to win. Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team. And that was simply the problem with Ronaldo.” He acknowledged Ronaldo’s influence among his teammates but insisted the forward’s performances had declined. “The players wanted to work for him and they looked up to him because let there be no misunderstanding about that. He is of course a tremendous player, one of the greats of all time. But that is also the reality over the last seven, eight years he simply can no longer deliver. From Juventus onwards it’s simply over. “And that is actually the great gift of Real Madrid — they always know when to say goodbye to players at the right moment. They recognise when a player’s level is declining and they say goodbye at a moment when to the outside world, they still appear to be at their peak. But they can no longer actually deliver.” Ronaldo was 36 when he returned to the Premier League, where his perceived inability to press opposition defenders attracted criticism from pundits and commentators. Ten Hag, however, argued that the issue went beyond the forward’s age, claiming he was no longer willing to push himself physically during training. “I naturally gave him a special status,” Ten Hag said. “I also went to him, I spoke to him prior to that job, I explained to him how we were going to play, what his role in that would be, what I expected of him, and what he could expect from me and from the team. But ultimately you also have to deliver yourself and he was no longer capable of pushing himself to the limit. “As I just said, he could no longer bring himself to push through the pain, to give everything every single day and to train at his maximum in order to get fit. item.content:encoded: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has criticised Cristiano Ronaldo’s fitness and commitment during their time together at Old Trafford, saying the Portuguese forward could “no longer deliver” at the highest level after leaving Juventus in 2021. Ten Hag, who is now the technical director of Dutch club FC Twente, made the remarks during an interview with ESPN NL’s Goedemorgen Eredivisie on Sunday, reflecting on his strained relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner. Ronaldo returned to Manchester United from Juventus in 2021 and scored 27 goals in 54 appearances under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ten Hag. However, his relationship with the Dutch manager deteriorated as he was frequently left out of the starting line-up. United eventually terminated his contract in November 2022 following his explosive interview with Piers Morgan, in which he said he felt “betrayed” by Ten Hag and criticised the club’s hierarchy. Reflecting on the challenges of managing the forward, Ten Hag said Ronaldo’s reluctance to put the team first created problems within the squad. “The challenge is to get the team functioning, really as always. Every player is important in that and you need top players to be able to win. Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must work for the team. And that was simply the problem with Ronaldo.” He acknowledged Ronaldo’s influence among his teammates but insisted the forward’s performances had declined. “The players wanted to work for him and they looked up to him because let there be no misunderstanding about that. He is of course a tremendous player, one of the greats of all time. But that is also the reality over the last seven, eight years he simply can no longer deliver. From Juventus onwards it’s simply over. “And that is actually the great gift of Real Madrid — they always know when to say goodbye to players at the right moment. They recognise when a player’s level is declining and they say goodbye at a moment when to the outside world, they still appear to be at their peak. But they can no longer actually deliver.” Ronaldo was 36 when he returned to the Premier League, where his perceived inability to press opposition defenders attracted criticism from pundits and commentators. Ten Hag, however, argued that the issue went beyond the forward’s age, claiming he was no longer willing to push himself physically during training. “I naturally gave him a special status,” Ten Hag said. “I also went to him, I spoke to him prior to that job, I explained to him how we were going to play, what his role in that would be, what I expected of him, and what he could expect from me and from the team. But ultimately you also have to deliver yourself and he was no longer capable of pushing himself to the limit. “As I just said, he could no longer bring himself to push through the pain, to give everything every single day and to train at his maximum in order to get fit. And if you’re not fit in the Premier League, Champions League, or with the Portuguese national team, well, then you simply have no chance.” Asked about Ronaldo’s reputation for exceptional dedication to physical fitness, Ten Hag said the perception did not entirely reflect the situation during their time together. “That’s not entirely true, but that is the image. And that is of course how he became so good. But ultimately he could no longer bring himself to do that. “If you can’t do it, well, then the laws of the Premier League are merciless. Then you can no longer keep up, you are no longer able to get into the box. He can still finish a chance, you still see that. But to get into that power and intensity of the Premier League, that’s no longer possible. For that you need to be fit.” The former United manager also dismissed suggestions that Ronaldo’s goals had changed his assessment of the forward’s performances, saying the player arrived late for pre-season preparations. “That didn’t happen because he arrived very late due to personal circumstances. By then the season had already started and things went wrong straight away. He wasn’t fit and couldn’t deliver.” Despite his criticism, Ten Hag praised Ronaldo’s contribution to football but maintained that he had to make decisions in the interest of Manchester United. He also compared the forward’s approach to that of Argentina captain Lionel Messi, arguing that even the greatest players must prioritise their teams. “No one is bigger than a club or a country,” Ten Hag said. “Not even Cristiano Ronaldo and not even Messi. In the end, the team always comes first. And so, as I just said, every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must yield to the team. And if he no longer does that, well then it can’t be a success and it will never become a success. Then it simply stops. “That is also what’s remarkable about Messi — how he worked at Argentina. That was fantastic to see. But that also required a big investment from Messi himself. Ultimately everyone went along with it and everyone worked for him but he of course gave an enormous amount back.” Ten Hag’s latest comments come after Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese Football Federation following his walkout on the national team during the October international break. He was also fined €255 but has indicated his willingness to represent Portugal again. The Dutchman also addressed his departure from Manchester United, dismissing suggestions of bitterness towards the club. Asked whether restrictions surrounding his exit had prevented him from speaking publicly for two years, Ten Hag said: “I was allowed to give interviews, but not to damage the club. But I wouldn’t have done that anyway — that goes without saying. “United gave me so much and I worked there with such great pleasure, with the people. [We] simply had a fantastic relationship, built fantastic connections. And the fans, such fantastic moments in those FA Cup finals, League Cup, [they] always supported. So there’s no bitterness.” Vanguard News The post “He could no longer deliver” – Ten Hag explains why Ronaldo struggled at Man United appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Flock keeps ignoring requests to cancel its contracts
item.description: While more cities are canceling their contracts with Flock Safety, just as many are discovering how difficult that can be in some instances. Plymouth, Minnesota's city council voted to terminate its contract with Flock in September, but failed to respond to the city's request. For over a month, the cameras remained up, and the city had received no acknowledgment from the company. So, Police Chief Eric Fadden took matters into his own hands and physically disconnected the cameras. "After hearing nothing for more than a week, I directed our staff to disconnect the power cords from the cameras in order to be sure that they are not functioning … Read the full story at The Verge.
