item.title: Arsenal End 14-Year Winless Run At Anfield To Go Top Of Premier League
item.description: Arsenal moved to the top of the Premier League with their first win away to Liverpool in 14 years as Kai Havertz’s early strike secured a 1-0 victory for the Gunners. The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title. Arsenal climbed three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But with City expected to be hit with a severe points penalty, unless they can overturn a guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League rules, Arsenal dealt a huge blow to their most likely rivals for the title. “It’s been such a long time without this feeling here, that we really needed it,” said Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta. “We are extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody has done.” Liverpool produced arguably their best spell of Andoni Iraola’s early months in charge with a blistering 30 minutes after conceding, but failed to take their chances as the Spaniard suffered just his second defeat in 14 games since arriving from Bournemouth. Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister (R) vies with Arsenal’s Norwegian midfielder #08 Martin Odegaard (2R) and Arsenal’s English midfielder #41 Declan Rice (L) during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks. The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions. Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross. The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back. Isak honesty saves Arsenal Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea. Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time. “I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down,” said Iraola. “I loved a lot of moments of the game. “We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. The defending champions were made to suffer after the German’s 16th-minute opener but held out for what could be a telling win in their quest to retain the title. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) Arteta was stinging in his criticism of the Arsenal side that crashed out to fourth-tier Fleetwood on Tuesday in one of the biggest ever League Cup shocks. The Arsenal boss got the response he desired in a strong start from the champions. Havertz was one of the biggest culprits for wasting chances in midweek but made amends with a simple finish from Declan Rice’s precise low cross. The early goal lit the touchpaper for a pulsating first 45 minutes as Liverpool roared back. Isak honesty saves Arsenal Iraola and Arteta played together as boys for Basque side Antiguoko Kirol Elkartea. Arteta’s old friend gave his side one of the most uncomfortable afternoons they have experienced in recent seasons as Arsenal’s rock-solid defence was left clinging on for half-time. “I loved the reaction from my players after going 1-0 down,” said Iraola. “I loved a lot of moments of the game. “We have to keep going. It is very early in the season. Arsenal are in the best of the situations but it is just the start of November today.” Liverpool’s Argentinian midfielder #10 Alexis Mac Allister indicates he’s been butted during the English Premier League football match between Liverpool and Arsenal at Anfield in Liverpool, north west England on November 1, 2026. (Photo by Darren Staples / AFP) All of Liverpool’s three £100 million-plus ($134 million) forwards started together and there are signs the relationship between Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola is beginning to flourish. Isak did Arsenal a favour by not going down as he was pulled back by Jurrien Timber when just failing to connect with a wicked delivery from Barcola. “The Alex one is a clear penalty,” added Iraola. “We can all see that he holds the shirt (but) because he doesn’t go to the floor, you are not going to call the penalty? I don’t understand it.” Wirtz curled a free-kick onto the bar from a narrow angle and Alexis Mac Allister should have buried a header into the goal rather than finding the stand behind David Raya’s goal. item.title: Breaking More Barriers, Bridging Wider Gaps: NITDA and ENGAUSA’s Journey Towards Inclusive Digital Transformation
item.description: Digital inclusion is not simply about providing computers, internet access or digital skills training. It is about breaking the barriers that prevent people from accessing opportunities, acquiring relevant competencies and participating meaningfully in the digital economy. For almost seven years, under the visionary leadership of Engr. Mustapha Habu Ringim, ENGAUSA GLOBAL TECH HUB LTD has consistently demonstrated this philosophy through its innovative, multilingual and inclusive approach to technology education, skills development, entrepreneurship and human capital development. Three major public-sector contributors to this journey, through their respective mandates, have been the National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI), under the leadership of Dr. Kazim Kolawole Raji; the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), under the impactful leadership of Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi; and the Federal Ministry of Education, through the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), under the exemplary leadership of Prof. Idris Muhammad Bugaje. Other important Federal Government stakeholders include the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) and the National Directorate of Employment (NDE). I will soon dedicate separate blog posts to celebrating the contributions of each of these key stakeholders, as well as other partners from both the public and private sectors. Our impactful relationship with NITDA, particularly in advancing digital inclusion, dates back to 2020, when the Agency recognised the grassroots impact of ENGAUSA’s digital inclusion programmes and incentivised our innovation hub with computers. This support was subsequently extended through the provision of smartphone repair tools, partnering in the national and local training programs and graduation ceremonies, further strengthening our capacity to deliver practical, industry-relevant training. Beyond these material contributions, NITDA’s confidence in ENGAUSA®’s experience and grassroots impact has also been reflected in the Agency’s repeated engagement of our Hub in policy development and strategic framework review processes. We have participated in several stakeholder consultations and workshops relating to key national initiatives, including the Nigeria Startup Policy, the National Digital Literacy Framework (NDLF) and the Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme. These engagements have provided opportunities for ENGAUSA® to contribute practical insights from its experience in inclusive digital skills development, grassroots innovation, entrepreneurship and human capital development. The results speak for themselves. item.content:encoded: Digital inclusion is not simply about providing computers, internet access or digital skills training. It is about breaking the barriers that prevent people from accessing opportunities, acquiring relevant competencies and participating meaningfully in the digital economy. For almost seven years, under the visionary leadership of Engr. Mustapha Habu Ringim, ENGAUSA GLOBAL TECH HUB LTD has consistently demonstrated this philosophy through its innovative, multilingual and inclusive approach to technology education, skills development, entrepreneurship and human capital development. Three major public-sector contributors to this journey, through their respective mandates, have been the National Board for Technology Incubation (NBTI), under the leadership of Dr. Kazim Kolawole Raji; the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), under the impactful leadership of Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi; and the Federal Ministry of Education, through the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE), under the exemplary leadership of Prof. Idris Muhammad Bugaje. Other important Federal Government stakeholders include the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) and the National Directorate of Employment (NDE). I will soon dedicate separate blog posts to celebrating the contributions of each of these key stakeholders, as well as other partners from both the public and private sectors. Our impactful relationship with NITDA, particularly in advancing digital inclusion, dates back to 2020, when the Agency recognised the grassroots impact of ENGAUSA’s digital inclusion programmes and incentivised our innovation hub with computers. This support was subsequently extended through the provision of smartphone repair tools, partnering in the national and local training programs and graduation ceremonies, further strengthening our capacity to deliver practical, industry-relevant training. Beyond these material contributions, NITDA’s confidence in ENGAUSA®’s experience and grassroots impact has also been reflected in the Agency’s repeated engagement of our Hub in policy development and strategic framework review processes. We have participated in several stakeholder consultations and workshops relating to key national initiatives, including the Nigeria Startup Policy, the National Digital Literacy Framework (NDLF) and the Three Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme. These engagements have provided opportunities for ENGAUSA® to contribute practical insights from its experience in inclusive digital skills development, grassroots innovation, entrepreneurship and human capital development. The results speak for themselves. ENGAUSA’s six-year impact journey has contributed to reaching over 11,000 beneficiaries, creating more than 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, and supporting the establishment and growth of over 1,000 startup businesses, SMEs and freelance enterprises across 22 states of Nigeria. 2022 Graduation Ceremony of 1,353 ENGAUSA® Trainees, Delivered in Collaboration with NITDA. NITDA has recognised these contributions through two major national recognitions within four years. The first was the Best Trainer of the Year Award in 2022, presented during the Digital Nigeria Conference. The second was the recent special recognition award presented during the Digital Literacy Workshop organised by NITDA on 20 October 2026, in recognition of ENGAUSA®’s outstanding contributions to digital inclusion and employment among the 252 Digital Literacy Centres registered on NITDA’s National Digital Literacy Dashboard. These recognitions affirm the importance of sustained institutional support for organisations delivering measurable impact at the grassroots. One of the most important lessons from our nearly seven years of programme implementation and impact assessment is that language inclusion is far more than a teaching technique. It is a powerful instrument for breaking barriers to education, technology and economic participation. By using Hausa alongside English in our learning environment, ENGAUSA has demonstrated that people should not be denied access to technical knowledge simply because they are not proficient in the dominant language of instruction. This approach has helped expand inclusion across several dimensions, including disability, gender, age, culture, education, economic circumstances and geographical location. It has created more accessible learning opportunities for persons with physical, sensory and other educational support needs; expanded opportunities for women and girls to acquire technical and entrepreneurial skills; and brought children, young people and adults into shared learning environments. It has also enabled learners from diverse cultural and traditional backgrounds to participate confidently while opening pathways for Almajiris, out-of-school children and young people, school dropouts and people with little or no formal educational qualifications. By reducing the cost barriers to acquiring employable and entrepreneurial skills and extending opportunities beyond conventional urban and formal educational environments, the approach has made skills development more accessible to underserved communities. Our experience also reinforces an important policy position: language-related barriers deserve explicit recognition as educational accessibility concerns. While language disadvantage is not itself a disability, it can prevent learners, including persons with disabilities, from understanding, communicating and participating fully in education and skills development. No learner should be left behind because of language or disability. The ENGAUSA experience has also contributed to changing perceptions about the value of technical competencies. Through competency-based training, recognition of prior learning, practical mentoring and enterprise incubation, we have promoted the dignity of skills and the formalisation of informal businesses. Our programmes have opened doors for people with zero certificates, Almajiris, unemployed and underemployed university graduates, women, freelancers and online workers. Many have progressed from learners to competent technicians, independent service providers, business owners and employers of labour. Some graduates have gone further to become multipliers of opportunity, reaching thousands of other beneficiaries through their own training, mentoring, business activities and community engagements. More than 11,000 people have benefited from ENGAUSA®’s highly subsidised skills acquisition programmes and 100% scholarship opportunities supported by partner organisations and individual philanthropists. Perhaps one of our most remarkable achievements is the creation of learning environments where people from different educational, socioeconomic, religious, traditional and cultural backgrounds sit together, learn together and build their futures without stereotypes or discrimination. In line with our commitment to leaving no one behind, ENGAUSA®’s inclusive approach also creates learning opportunities for persons with hearing and visual impairments. Through appropriate learning adaptations and available assistive technologies, we strive to ensure that these learners are not excluded from acquiring relevant digital and technical skills. We recognise, however, that access to specialised assistive and adaptive technologies remains a major challenge, as such tools are still unavailable in many digital inclusion centres across the country. This underscores the need to prioritise accessible learning infrastructure, assistive technologies and specialised training support. More importantly, these provisions must be treated as high-priority requirements, not afterthoughts, in the design and implementation of educational curricula, National Occupational Standards, competency frameworks and national policies. item.title: 2027: Political permutations favour Tinubu – Deputy Senate President
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau Jibrin, APC, Kano North has expressed optimism that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will emerge victorious in the January 16, 2027, presidential election, citing assessments by political analysts and the prevailing political situation in the country. Senator Barau spoke at the weekend during the inauguration of campaign committees for Dawakin Tofa, Tofa and Rimin Gado Local Government Areas of Kano State, where he charged party members to work collectively towards securing victory for all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the forthcoming general elections. In a statement signed on Sunday by his Special Adviser, Media and Publicity, Ismail Mudashir, the Deputy President of the Senate said the foundation laid by President Tinubu during his first term would, by the grace of Allah, yield the desired results in his second term. Barau Jibrin who expressed appreciation to party leaders, elected representatives, local government chairmen, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and other stakeholders for their support and commitment to the APC, assured them that the unity and cooperation currently enjoyed by the party would be sustained. “Based on the assessments of political analysts and the current state of Nigerian politics, all indications suggest that, by Allah’s grace, Bola Ahmed Tinubu will win the presidential election,” he said. He noted that Kano, being one of the largest states in the country and second only to Lagos in terms of the latest registered voters, deserved greater attention and opportunities from the Federal Government. According to him, the Governor’s decision to lead the people from the New Nigeria People’s Party (NNPP) to the APC was a strategic move that have enhanced Kano’s political relevance and improved its access to developmental opportunities. The Deputy President of the Senate expressed confidence that the political unity achieved in Kano would translate into tangible benefits for the people, particularly with the alignment of councillors, local government chairmen, state legislators, members of the National Assembly and the Governor under the APC. He added that the coming elections would usher in a new phase of political and developmental activities, with elected representatives expected to contribute meaningfully to the development of their respective constituencies. Senator Barau explained that the campaign committees were carefully constituted to accommodate party leaders, members of the party’s executive committees, former and serving legislators, councillors, local government chairmen, new party members and respected elders. He urged members of the committees to take their responsibilities seriously and mobilise effectively for the APC ahead of the elections. “What is required of you is to play your part actively in securing victory. Mobilise, campaign and ensure that all APC candidates emerge victoriously from top to bottom. May Allah grant us

item.title: 2027: ‘We’ll not allow rigging’ — Dino Melaye warns INEC
item.description: Former Kogi West senator, Dino Melaye, has accused the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of taking steps to rig the 2027 general elections, warning that any attempt to manipulate the polls would be resisted. Melaye made the allegation in a post on his X handle on Sunday, claiming that recent activities by the electoral body suggest what he described as “anticipatory rigging”. “The activities of INEC in recent times point at anticipatory rigging. Which will be resisted,” Melaye wrote. The former lawmaker also called on INEC to redeem its image ahead of the 2027 elections, insisting that Nigerians would not tolerate electoral manipulation. “INEC must be born again this time because we will not allow rigging. Rig and say your final prayer,” he added. Melaye, a chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has remained a vocal critic of the electoral commission since the 2023 general elections. His comments come amid controversy over the discovery of AI-generated photographs in INEC’s preliminary voters’ register, as well as complaints by political parties over the omission of some candidates from the commission’s final list. Vanguard News The post 2027: ‘We’ll not allow rigging’ — Dino Melaye warns INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: ADC-PCC challenges Tinubu to defend failure to deliver electricity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his failure to deliver on his 2023 electricity pledge, insisting that he should not seek re-election without fulfilling the promise. The council said Nigerians had not forgotten Tinubu’s categorical declaration during the 2023 presidential campaign that they should not vote for him for a second term if he failed to deliver electricity, dismissing attempts by the APC to reinterpret his words as an afterthought. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC was reacting to comments by Dele Alake, spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, defending the President’s electricity record. “Don’t vote for me for second term if I fail to deliver electricity,” the President had told Nigerians during the 2023 campaign. The opposition campaign council argued that more than three years after the pledge, Nigerians were still grappling with persistent power outages, repeated national grid collapses and inadequate electricity supply. It accused the Tinubu administration of increasing the financial burden on consumers through higher electricity bills, discriminatory tariff classifications and continued estimated billing, despite the much-publicised Presidential Metering Initiative. The council also said businesses, including hotels and other hospitality facilities, had resorted to rationing electricity by switching off power for guests during daytime hours to reduce operating costs. Dismissing the administration’s reliance on the Electricity Act and bond programmes to defend its record, the ADC-PCC insisted that policy documents and financial instruments could not substitute for actual electricity supply. “An Act is not electricity. A bond prospectus does not power homes and factories. Nigerians cannot eat statutes. What Nigerians need is electricity that works, not another round of explanations and publicity,” the council said. It further accused the administration of imposing higher tariffs without ensuring reliable supply, leaving households, manufacturers and small businesses to contend with rising operating costs. The ADC-PCC also questioned the implementation of the Presidential Metering Initiative, alleging that electricity distribution companies continued to impose estimated bills on consumers. “The President’s own condition for seeking a second term was straightforward: deliver electricity or do not ask Nigerians for another mandate,” the council maintained. It urged the APC to address the President’s 2023 commitment directly, rather than attempt to dilute his words, warning that the administration’s electricity record would be a major issue as Nigerians prepare to decide whether to renew Tinubu’s mandate in the January 16, 2027 election. The post 2027: ADC-PCC challenges Tinubu to defend failure to deliver electricity appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: In Photos: Senegal Makes History as the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Kick Off
item.description: Khaby Lame and Boubou Niang take the stage with a young participant at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. If you have been keeping an eye on sports and global pop culture, history was made over the weekend in West Africa. Senegal officially kicked off the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games with a spectacular opening ceremony at the 55,000-capacity Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, marking the first time an Olympic event has ever taken place on African soil. Running through to 13 November, the Games are bringing together over 2,600 young athletes aged 14 to 17, competing across 25 sports and 153 medal events. The action spans three vibrant hubs: the historic capital city of Dakar, the modern satellite city of Diamniadio, and the coastal resort area of Saly. Host nation Senegal enters the arena during the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Parade of Nations. Under the official motto “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”, the opening ceremony turned into a celebration of music, dance, visual arts, and storytelling. Beyond the parade of nations, the night showcased iconic West African talent. Senegalese music legend Baaba Maal led a massive musical tribute alongside Kiné Lam and hip-hop outfit Daara J Family , while Gambian kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh and social media star Khaby Lame made featured appearances. Massamba Gueye performs during a cultural heritage sequence at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Nigeria also took centre stage during the ceremony, with spoken word poet Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , delivering a live performance surrounded by dancers against a backdrop of stadium lights. Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. The Games feature an exciting, youth-focused sports lineup including 3×3 basketball, futsal, beach volleyball, rugby sevens, breakdancing, street skateboarding, wushu, beach wrestling, table tennis, and archery. Over 200 National Olympic Committees are participating—with strong contingents representing African nations like host nation Senegal, Nigeria,South Africa, Kenya, and Algeria, alongside global delegations including Great Britain, Australia, Germany, Argentina, South Korea, and the United States. With two full weeks of sporting events, cultural showcases, and youth competition ahead, Senegal has set the tone for a historic milestone in African sports and lifestyle history. Massamba Gueye performs during a cultural heritage sequence at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Choreographed dance troupe in yellow satin performing at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Team Japan athlete delegation marching during the Parade of Nations at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. The Burkina Faso delegation marching during the Parade of Nations at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. item.title: Mbappe Scores After China Controversy As Madrid Beat Santander
item.description: Kylian Mbappe moved on from a tumultuous week by scoring a penalty to help Real Madrid win 3-0 at Racing Santander on Sunday. The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout. Real Madrid’s Ivorian forward #25 Yan Diomande (C) celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Spanish league football match between Racing de Santander and Real Madrid CF at El Sardinero Stadium in Santander on November 1, 2026. (Photo by ANDER GILLENEA / AFP) Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday. Jose Mourinho’s side have won six straight games across all competitions and are a point behind city rivals Atletico Madrid, who beat Levante 2-0. “In the first half we were very strong; we came out to play well,” Mourinho told reporters. “The team is growing and playing well; I think we should have scored even more goals with the chances we had.” Mbappe won a soft penalty as he went down under little pressure from Matteo Prati, smashing it home to put Madrid ahead at the Sardinero stadium in the 11th minute. It was the 27-year-old’s 12th league goal of the season, trailing only Barcelona’s Raphinha with 15 in the scoring charts. Madrid had control of the game, and a fine pass from Arda Guler sent Bellingham through on goal for the second. The England international knocked the ball past the goalkeeper and rolled home for his 50th goal since joining Madrid in 2023. Guler spun a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid’s record-signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box. The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players. Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala. Racing won a penalty after Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review. Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net, and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance. Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign. Earlier, Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table. “(Madrid’s penalty award) annoys me,” Racing coach Jose Alberto told DAZN. “Evidently we came across a great Madrid, who put us under a lot of pressure in the first half hour and were much better than us, but what conditions? Everything was the first goal and the penalty.” Later, on Sun

item.title: APM Members Defect To PDP In Katsina, Back Danmarke’s Governorship Bid
item.description: At least 5,000 members of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Katsina State have reportedly joined the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), pledging support for the party’s governorship candidate, Senator Yakubu Lado Danmarke, ahead of the 2027 elections. The defectors, led by the Chairman of Katsina Frontiers, Alhaji Aliyu Sani, formally joined the PDP at a rally in Katsina on Sunday. Sani said the decision followed the group’s confidence in Danmarke’s leadership qualities and record of humanitarian support, particularly for the poor, vulnerable, elderly and children. He cited the senator’s provision of food and cash assistance, especially during Ramadan, describing him as a humble and compassionate leader who puts the welfare of the people above personal comfort and material wealth. Also speaking at the rally, Muhammad Hassan El-Makki said Katsina needed a leader genuinely committed to the well-being of its people. He described Danmarke as experienced and capable of transforming agriculture, healthcare, energy and infrastructure, while pointing to his scholarship programmes and contributions to community development. El-Makki urged residents to support the senator’s governorship ambition, describing him as “tested and trusted” in humanitarian service. In his remarks, Danmarke thanked the new members for joining the PDP, saying their defection reflected growing confidence in the party and his candidacy. He said the new entrants included political structures associated with a former governorship aspirant, prominent personalities, retirees and grassroots coordinators from across the state. Danmarke identified insecurity as Katsina’s most pressing challenge, pledging to make restoring security his administration’s immediate priority if elected. He also promised to revive the education, health, agriculture and infrastructure sectors, while accusing the incumbent administration of failing to meet the expectations of residents. The PDP candidate called on the people of Katsina to join what he described as the party’s movement for change, promising people-centred governance and a rebuilding of the state. The state PDP Chairman, Alhaji Nura Amadi Kurfi, gave the vote of thanks, expressing confidence that Lado’s candidacy would usher in progress and development in Katsina. The post APM Members Defect To PDP In Katsina, Back Danmarke’s Governorship Bid appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Should Premier League strugglers stick or twist as pressure on managers mounts? | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Unusually, all clubs in the top flight have the same manager with whom they began the season – but the first sacking may not be far away No Premier League manager has yet lost his job this season. In only three of the past 10 campaigns was November reached without a club making a managerial change. The 2026-27 season commencing with 11 managers who were appointed at some point in 2026 has probably contributed to the early season stability. They have to be given a chance to fashion their side as they see fit. But with roughly a quarter of the season played and only one more round of fixtures before an international break, the first sacking may not be far away. Continue reading...

item.title: 2027: Don’t disrupt opposition campaigns — Otti warns supporters
item.description: By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has cautioned supporters of the Labour Party against taking the law into their hands or interfering with the campaign activities of rival political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor warned that no political affiliation would shield anyone from arrest for disrupting the lawful activities of opposition parties, stressing that political competition must be conducted within the ambit of the law. Otti spoke on Sunday in Umuahia while formally flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he declared that his administration would not tolerate political intolerance or the denial of opponents’ democratic rights. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadiums, provided they complied with established procedures, obtained necessary approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Reiterating his position, the governor said security agencies had been instructed to ensure that no political group was prevented from holding legitimate rallies or other campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” Otti said. In a strong message to party loyalists, he warned against assuming that membership of the ruling party conferred immunity for acts capable of undermining the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond the conduct of campaigns, Otti challenged opposition parties to raise the quality of political debate by offering alternative policy directions rather than relying on personal attacks or recycling issues he said had been addressed by his administration. According to him, the political conversation in Abia should now be centred on development priorities and the next phase of governance rather than basic issues such as salaries, pensions, roads and environmental sanitation. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Okogba
item.content:encoded: By Steve Oko & Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA – Abia State Governor, Alex Otti, has cautioned supporters of the Labour Party against taking the law into their hands or interfering with the campaign activities of rival political parties ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governor warned that no political affiliation would shield anyone from arrest for disrupting the lawful activities of opposition parties, stressing that political competition must be conducted within the ambit of the law. Otti spoke on Sunday in Umuahia while formally flagging off the Labour Party’s 2027 campaign in the state, where he declared that his administration would not tolerate political intolerance or the denial of opponents’ democratic rights. He said opposition parties were free to use public facilities, including stadiums, provided they complied with established procedures, obtained necessary approvals and paid the stipulated fees. Reiterating his position, the governor said security agencies had been instructed to ensure that no political group was prevented from holding legitimate rallies or other campaign activities. “I have since given a public directive, and I am repeating it here, that opposition parties should not be restricted from the use of public facilities, including the stadium, once they apply and obtain the necessary approvals,” Otti said. In a strong message to party loyalists, he warned against assuming that membership of the ruling party conferred immunity for acts capable of undermining the democratic process. “You do not have my mandate to attack people or to stop people from campaigning. “Security agencies have been mandated to arrest and deal decisively with anyone who attempts to obstruct any political group from holding their legitimate activities, even if they are Labour Party members. I hope I am heard clearly,” he said. Beyond the conduct of campaigns, Otti challenged opposition parties to raise the quality of political debate by offering alternative policy directions rather than relying on personal attacks or recycling issues he said had been addressed by his administration. According to him, the political conversation in Abia should now be centred on development priorities and the next phase of governance rather than basic issues such as salaries, pensions, roads and environmental sanitation. “Do not forget that in Abia we have gone past the era of campaigning on the payment of salaries and pensions, construction of roads or urban sanitation. “The hygiene issues have been dealt with. If you are unable to raise your campaign pitch to the development realities of our state, you will definitely struggle to convince any informed voter,” the governor said. He urged political opponents to interrogate available performance data before making claims about the state, pointing to Abia’s ratings in the Citizen Satisfaction Index, State Performance Index and Fiscal Performance Ranking by governance-monitoring organisations. “You should go and do your research first before coming out to open your mouth, because there are data everywhere to show what has been achieved. Evidently, the world knows that Abia is on the right track,” Otti said. The governor also argued that the experiences of Abians within and outside the country had lent credibility to external assessments of the state’s development trajectory, adding that multilateral institutions had opened development assistance opportunities for Abia. “It would therefore be unthinkable that anyone will ever be allowed to return us to the old era of irresponsibility and misery,” he declared. Otti, who expressed appreciation to residents for their turnout at the campaign flag-off, called on party supporters to intensify grassroots mobilisation and take the message of the party to communities across the state. “This is your project, and as you return to the communities, knock on every door and remind our people that we still have a job to complete. Invite them to join the campaign so that together we can conclude the journey that began 12 years ago in faith and optimism,” he added. Highlight of the event was the presentation of the party flag to national and state house of assembly candidates of Labour Party for the 2027 polls. The event was massively attended by party members including the candidates for the various elections and their supporters who were competing for recognition as they chanted solidarity songs for their various candidates. item.title: France: Route du Rhum yacht race sets off
item.description: The 115 sailors competing in the Route du Rhum set sail from Saint-Malo on Sunday in mild weather, embarking on a solo transatlantic crossing. The race began at 12:02 GMT, with boats heading along the Brittany coast in light winds towards a mandatory checkpoint near Cap Fréhel, where crowds had gathered to watch. One competitor, Nicolas d’Estais, described the conditions as ideal before boarding his yacht, Café Joyeux. Selina Sykes reports from Saint-Malo.

item.title: Oleshky: Evacuations during first humanitarian truce of war end
item.description: A successful evacuation. Residents of the city of Oleshky who had requested to be evacuated were reunited with their loved ones in Ukraine on Saturday, October 31. The city, located on the front line and under Russian occupation, is facing a humanitarian crisis, with civilians lacking even the most basic necessities. A localised ceasefire has been in place since Tuesday. France 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze shares the latest.

Guler spurned a good opportunity for the third after being set up by Mbappe, before Madrid’s record signing Diomande lashed home from the edge of the box. The hosts started the second half well, pushing Madrid back, much to the chagrin of Mourinho, who yelled at his players. Madrid regained their control and racked up several more chances, with Mbappe hitting the post and Bellingham denied by Racing goalkeeper Julen Agirrezabala. Racing won a penalty after Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni handled in the box, but the award was cancelled after a VAR review. Bellingham had a second goal ruled out in stoppage time after he strayed offside before finding the net and Endrick bent an effort narrowly wide from distance. Hosts Racing, 16th, back in La Liga for the first time in 14 seasons, fell to their first home defeat of the campaign. Earlier Sevilla, sixth, suffered a 3-1 loss at Getafe, who moved into mid-table. Later Sunday Athletic Bilbao host Real Sociedad in a Basque derby and Valencia visit Elche. The French forward narrowly lost out on the Ballon d’Or to Bayern Munich’s Harry Kane on Monday and then had to apologise after a social media storm following a video in which he joked about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong. Real Madrid’s match, along with other Spanish fixtures this weekend, was not broadcast by Chinese state television because of the fallout. Jude Bellingham and Yan Diomande were also on target to keep third-place Madrid within three points of leaders Barcelona, who thrashed Alaves 6-1 on Saturday. item.title: Scottish roundup: Falkirk shock Celtic; Hibernian beat Hearts in semi-final
item.description: Pressure on Martin O’Neill after 2-0 defeat by Falkirk Hibs will face Rangers in Premier Sports Cup final Celtic slumped to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk on Sunday to ramp up the scrutiny on manager Martin O’Neill after a run of three wins in 10 games. The Scottish champions had the chance to extend their lead at the top of the table to seven points, but never recovered from conceding a third-minute opener to Ethan Ross. Scott Tanser scored a second before half-time and the Bairns even had a third goal ruled out by a video assistant referee review for handball against Jacob Murrell. The majority of Celtic’s struggles this season have come in European competition as they crashed out of the Champions League qualifiers and have lost all three Europa League group matches. item.title: 2027: ADC-PCC accuses Tinubu govt of plot to weaken opposition
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of orchestrating a campaign of intimidation and suppression against opposition parties to weaken them ahead of the 2027 general elections. The Council said the alleged attacks on opposition leaders, demolition of campaign offices, denial of campaign venues and harassment of party members were part of a coordinated effort to undermine political participation and democratic freedoms. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the campaign council cited attacks on its leaders and members in Kaduna, the reported assault on its Sokoto State governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya, by operatives of the Sokoto Marshals along Airport Road, Sokoto, and alleged attacks on other opposition figures. It also cited the reported demolition of its governorship campaign office in Kebbi State and the alleged denial of a campaign venue in Enugu State to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate, Mr Peter Obi. The Council further referenced reported attacks on the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, and other opposition voices, describing the incidents as evidence of growing political intolerance. “These are calculated atrocious actions skewed to scare Nigerians ahead of the general elections,” the statement said. The ADC-PCC warned that the alleged incidents posed a threat to political pluralism, insisting that no government could suppress the democratic aspirations of Nigerians indefinitely. It recalled that popular resistance contributed to the collapse of former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s third-term agenda, arguing that the same democratic forces would resist any attempt to restrict political participation. The Council said Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) had benefited from opposition politics when they were outside government, insisting that the same freedoms must be guaranteed to all political parties. It also expressed concern over the continued detention of its Vice Chairman and former Kaduna State governor, Mallam Nasir El-Rufai, alleging that he was being unlawfully held and denied bail. “The world is watching, and the burden of this illegality rests squarely on those responsible,” the Council stated. The campaign council further alleged that financial inducements were being used to compromise individuals and weaken opposition ranks, but insisted that Nigerians would not surrender their constitutional rights for monetary benefits. “President Tinubu is at liberty to corruptly buy a few consciences with money and material inducements. Millions of Naira are being offered to weak individuals to mortgage their rights, but not all Nigerians are for sale,” the statement declared. item.title: 6 Perfect Star Trek Episodes to Watch to Say Goodbye to Patrick Stewart
item.description: Even more significant than the quantity of Star Trek that Stewart made was the quality. Kirk is in many ways a classic pulp action hero. He faces conflicts head on, never afraid to throw a punch or flirt with a sexy alien. Picard represents a different form of masculinity, valuing compassion, knowledge, and communication above all else. He is the endlessly patient father figure for his crew, and for the next generation of Star Trek viewers, presiding over one of the most beautiful visions of what the future could look like. It’s that connection that has left fans in mourning following his death on Thursday at the age of 86.

item.title: 'Metroid Prime' needs some 'Resident Evil'-style remakes to rediscover its sci-fi shooter mojo
item.description: null Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. After five years in development at Retro Studios, the original makers of the Metroid Prime series, fans were greeted with annoying side characters, a bike for Samus to roam the barren landscape on, and a deeply unsatisfying ending. It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. Many franchises were jumping from 2D to 3D at the turn of the millennium, and there were plenty of failures — but Metroid wasn’t one of them. The two sequels would enhance how players control Samus with powerful weapons and a multiplayer mode, but the 18-year gap between Metroid Prime 3 and 4 left players expecting something special. Metroid Prime 4: Beyond’s average reception left fans wondering where the series can go next. It’s admittedly strange that Metroid Prime 2 and 3 have yet to debut on Nintendo Switch , either through the Nintendo Online service or as remasters. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has just dropped for Switch 2, and seeing Nintendo leverage one of the best games of all time for a modern take has given us an idea: let's give the Metroid Prime trilogy the remake treatment, taking inspiration from Capcom’s efforts with Resident Evil. To Prime and Beyond (Image credit: Nintendo) From 2002’s Resident Evil remake to the more recent successes with Resident Evil 2 & 4, Capcom has managed to recreate the feeling and survival horror tropes of the originals while modernizing the gameplay. Whether it's the constant tension of being stalked by a Terminator-like Mr. X in 2019’s Resident Evil 2, or the palpable paranoia you feel exploring in Resident Evil 4 — the skin might be new, but the bones are undeniably "Resi." Even recently-announced Resident Evil: Veronica — whilst a remake of 1999’s Code: Veronica — looks set to be a brand new take that evokes the feeling of the original game, but brings it into the modern era. Prime 4 felt like a game out of time. Sure, it looked the part, but it felt decidedly like a GameCube game. So why not take a leaf out of Capcom's book, apply their "recapturing the vibes" mindset for a Metroid Prime Trilogy Remake, using the Prime 4 engine as its foundation. 2023’s Metroid Prime Remastered showed off the venerable title with better textures and widescreen support, but a remake powered by the fourth game’s engine could showcase the opening and Tallon IV in a whole new light. (Image credit: Nintendo) Similar to 2002’s Resident Evil Remake with the Spencer Mansion, places would feel familiar but fresh, thanks to updated graphics, better sound, and support for HD Rumble 2 that could help the player become more immersed in the game. And of course, you can change a few things to play off people's expectations. If Nintendo is feeling brave, the reimagining could even begin at the end of Zero Missi

item.content:encoded: null Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. The two sequels would enhance how players control Samus with powerful weapons and a multiplayer mode, but the 18-year gap between Metroid Prime 3 and 4 left players expecting something special. Metroid Prime 4: Beyond’s average reception left fans wondering where the series can go next. It’s admittedly strange that Metroid Prime 2 and 3 have yet to debut on Nintendo Switch , either through the Nintendo Online service or as remasters. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has just dropped for Switch 2, and seeing Nintendo leverage one of the best games of all time for a modern take has given us an idea: let's give the Metroid Prime trilogy the remake treatment, taking inspiration from Capcom’s efforts with Resident Evil. To Prime and Beyond (Image credit: Nintendo) From 2002’s Resident Evil remake to the more recent successes with Resident Evil 2 & 4, Capcom has managed to recreate the feeling and survival horror tropes of the originals while modernizing the gameplay. Whether it's the constant tension of being stalked by a Terminator-like Mr. X in 2019’s Resident Evil 2, or the palpable paranoia you feel exploring in Resident Evil 4 — the skin might be new, but the bones are undeniably "Resi." Even recently-announced Resident Evil: Veronica — whilst a remake of 1999’s Code: Veronica — looks set to be a brand new take that evokes the feeling of the original game, but brings it into the modern era. Prime 4 felt like a game out of time. Sure, it looked the part, but it felt decidedly like a GameCube game. So why not take a leaf out of Capcom's book, apply their "recapturing the vibes" mindset for a Metroid Prime Trilogy Remake, using the Prime 4 engine as its foundation. 2023’s Metroid Prime Remastered showed off the venerable title with better textures and widescreen support, but a remake powered by the fourth game’s engine could showcase the opening and Tallon IV in a whole new light. (Image credit: Nintendo) Similar to 2002’s Resident Evil Remake with the Spencer Mansion, places would feel familiar but fresh, thanks to updated graphics, better sound, and support for HD Rumble 2 that could help the player become more immersed in the game. And of course, you can change a few things to play off people's expectations. If Nintendo is feeling brave, the reimagining could even begin at the end of Zero Mission, which is set just before Metroid Prime. Controlling Samus with all her abilities, facing off against Mother Brain in an area not seen in 3D, could be a great introduction to old and new players, as well as giving the opportunity to remake an area from a previous title. Then, players could escape to Samus’ ship, with the ability to pilot it to the Orpheron ship, where Prime begins. The Return of Metroid Prime Multiplayer (Image credit: Nintendo) A remake (or remakes) would obviously mean a big step-up in graphics and gameplay across all three games, but it could also herald the long-awaited return of its multiplayer mode from Metroid Prime 2, something that Metroid Prime 4: Beyond bizarrely left out. Up to four players could take part in one of two modes here - Deathmatch and Bounty Mode, which had players compete against one another by collecting coins to win matches. There were four arenas to choose from, with an additional two to unlock when players got far enough in Prime 2’s single-player mode. It was a fun time, and its absence in Prime 4: Beyond felt like a big miss, especially with the prospect of playing this mode online with others and using the Switch 2 features like Game Chat. A remake could fix this injustice, and even expand on the concept by offering new multiplayer modes alongside maps based on locations from across the Prime series. You could even add a co-op mode for the campaign, and a horde mode for co-op fans to enjoy online too. Give Samus the Itchy Tasty Treatment (Image credit: Nintendo) As it stands in 2026, the Metroid series feels adrift once more. Metroid Prime 4: Beyond will be lost to the sands of time, a mediocre entry in a series filled with bangers. As the latest Nintendo Direct eagerly showcased Donkey Kong, Zelda, and plenty of third-party releases, Samus was notably absent. Sure, she's just had a game, but it's hard not to be nervous after the drought that Metroid players had to suffer in the 2010s. Capcom was in a similar lull after 2012’s disappointing Resident Evil 6, a bloated and confusing entry that made players fear the end of the series. But the seventh entry, alongside the Resident Evil 2 Remake in 2019, breathed new life into the franchise, which has proved as tough to kill as any of Umbrella's bioweapons. Metroid's fate feels equally in the balance right now, and in a world where game studios are closing down and rivals like Microsoft are shrinking their focus to big-hitter franchises, Nintendo could easily let Metroid fall back into obscurity. Refocusing on what makes the series iconic is the key to its success, and modern remakes of the originals might just be what they need to rediscover that Metroid magic. There are some easy wins out there to keep fans engaged; it’d still be great to see more games appear on the Nintendo Online service, like Metroid Prime 2, and we'd love more 2D entries after the excellent Metroid Dread, but nothing hits like Prime, and Prime isn't hitting right now. If not, then I fear Samus will be riding her Vi-O-La into the sunset, deep within the barren wasteland of Sol Valley for the foreseeable future.

item.title: NDLEA intercepts large consignments of illicit drugs in 7 states
item.description: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has intercepted large consignments of illicit drugs in seven states across the country. The states include Lagos, Kano, Kaduna, Sokoto, Ondo, Oyo and Edo, in a series of intelligence-led operations. This is contained in a statement by the Director, Media and Advocacy, NDLEA, Mr Femi Babafemi on Sunday in Abuja. Breaking down the operation, Babafemi said NDLEA operatives, acting on actionable intelligence about the movement of skunk, intercepted a white Volkswagen LT 28 bus along Kudirat Abiola Way, Ikeja, Lagos. Babafemi said the NDLEA operatives intercepted 537kg of skunk, a potent strain of cannabis, on Sunday, Oct. 25, while it was being transported from the Island to the Mainland. “The same day, another team of officers intercepted a brown J5 bus along the Gbagada–Oshodi expressway, with 439 kilograms of the same substance seized,”he said. In Oyo, NDLEA operatives on Thursday conducted a follow-up operation at Idere road, Igboora, where two suspects were arrested. Babafemi said that their arrest came while loading 554 kilograms of skunk into a Volvo truck for onward movement into town. “The operation targeted a notorious drug dealer known as ‘Omo Oba’, who escaped arrest on October 25. “This happened when officers seized 309.5 kilograms of the strong cannabis strain popularly called ‘Ghanaian Loud’ linked to him,” he said. Also, in Kano, NDLEA operatives on Monday raided a location in Tsamiya area of Gezawa where they recovered 247,500 tablets of diazepam weighing 57.7 kilograms and 100,000 tablets of Exol-5 weighing 38.7 kilograms. “Two days later, on Wednesday, October 28, another team of officers stormed Dorayi area of the state, where they arrested two suspects with 19,250 pills of tramadol 225mg weighing 13.6 kilograms,” Babafemi said. According to him, in a raid at Tashan Banke area of the state, officers also arrested seven suspects and recovered 178.85 kilograms of cannabis alongside quantities of diazepam, tramadol, Exol-5 and pregabalin. In Ondo State, NDLEA operatives, on Oct. 25 acting on credible intelligence, raided cannabis farms in Ijare forest. Babafemi said that they arrested four suspects, adding that a total of 16 bags of processed cannabis weighing 180 kilograms were recovered from the farms. Similarly, a team of NDLEA operatives supported by soldiers on Wednesday raided Eko Camp in Ilushi, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State. Babafemi said that a cannabis plantation measuring 1.646 hectares with an estimated yield of 4,115.53 kilograms was destroyed. “A 50-year-old woman was arrested at the camp with 301 kilograms of processed cannabis, while another 176 kilograms of the drug was recovered during the raid,”he said. In Sokoto, operatives of Zone 7 Command of NDLEA, acting on credible intelligence, on Saturday arrested a 68-year-old man with 236.6 kilograms of skunk The post NDLEA intercepts large consignments of illicit drugs in 7 states appeared first on Van

item.title: A fully playable version of Portal prequel F-Stop leaked
item.description: Leakers have pieced together a playable version of the canceled Portal prequel F-Stop . Most of the assets came from the massive 12-terabyte leak that dropped this August. That didn't include the game's source code or map data, but those final pieces apparently hit the Valve Cut Content Discord this week, allowing a nearly complete version to be pieced together. Some dialog and elements of F-Stop eventually found their way into Portal 2 . But it differs dramatically from the mainline Portal games in that it's built around a camera mechanic that lets you capture an item by taking its picture and place it elsewhere using the resulting Polaroid … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
item.description: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. This illustration is a detection map showing a regional seismo-acoustic network in south-central and interior Alaska. Only stations with available data during the fireball event are shown. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.) item.dc:creator: Leonard David
item.content:encoded: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. This illustration is a detection map showing a regional seismo-acoustic network in south-central and interior Alaska. Only stations with available data during the fireball event are shown. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.) Location, time and estimated energy "For many fireballs, U.S. Government detections reported through NASA's CNEOS database provide an important starting point by establishing that an event occurred and, in many cases, providing basic parameters such as location, time and estimated energy," explained Elizabeth Silber, a senior research and development physicist at the U.S. Department of Energy's Sandia National Laboratories in New Mexico. "Civil and scientific observing systems can then add independent measurements that help refine and validate that initial characterization," said Silber. CNEOS, which is based at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, is NASA's center for computing asteroid and comet orbits and their odds of striking Earth. CNEOS computes high-precision orbits for such objects in support of NASA's Planetary Defense Coordination Office. Different and complementary information "The Alaska event is an especially useful example, because it was not reported by U.S. Government sensors in the CNEOS database. In this case, the event was reconstructed almost entirely from civil and scientific observations," Silber told Space.com. She said that the seismic and infrasound data constrained the trajectory and acoustic energy, the video provided independent optical information, and the weather radar detected material from the fireball falling to Earth. "So, the real strength is that these systems provide different and complementary information," said Silber. "When a U.S. Government detection is available, civil data can independently validate it and add much more detail. When one is not available, as in this case [for Alaska], the civil networks can still provide a surprisingly complete reconstruction." The May 20, 2023 Queensland superbolide caught on camera by ground-based optical observations. These are selected frames from Australia's Paddys Green station showing the evolution of the event. Frame (a) displays the initial entry. Frames (b) and (c) illustrate the rapid increase in luminosity, leading to severe sensor saturation. Frame (d) shows the final stages of the trajectory. (Image credit: Elizabeth Silber, et al.) Independent view The Alaska study shows how valuable it is to put together diverse types of observations once an event has occurred, said Silber. Each measurement responds to a different part of the event. "Seismic and infrasound sensors record the atmospheric shock waves and can constrain the trajectory, fragmentation and energy," she added. "Optical observations provide an independent view of the luminous flight. Doppler weather radar can detect surviving material after it has slowed and entered dark flight." Bottom line: no single sensor tells you everything. "Combining independent observations lets us move from simply knowing that an event occurred to determining how the object traveled through the atmosphere, where it fragmented, how much energy it released, and whether material may have survived to the ground," said Silber. Artist's rendering of NOAA's GOES East satellite in orbit. The spacecraft provides real-time mapping of lightning activity, among other duties. (Image credit: NOAA) 'Hard rain' is gonna fall Researchers got pretty lucky with the April 1, 2026 event over the South Atlantic, according to NASA's Rob Landis, a planetary defense specialist: Two civilian spacecraft located at different locations in geosynchronous orbit allowed them to conduct a rather unique investigation of this bolide. "With two civilian resources, we can actually discuss things more openly," Landis, who's now a visiting vehicle integration manager for the International Space Station at NASA's Johnson Space Center , told Space.com. Lightning-watching instruments not designed for detecting bolides, he said, "afford the science community to discuss these events and these sensors in a forthright, open manner. These lightning imagers give us opportunistic bonus science for those who study the 'hard rain.'" Landis said that, in his personal view, there's a lot of smaller stuff getting through the atmosphere. "To the casual observer, these certainly produce wonderful natural fireworks and are mostly harmless," Landis said. But, he stressed, it's important to be able to distinguish between natural events and human-made ones. "It would be a horrific tragedy if any nation responded to a natural event — if they misinterpret it as a preemptive strike," cautioned Landis. Sandia intern Logan Scamfer checks data recorded by a ground sensor in Alaska. Scamfer works with Sandia physicist Elizabeth Silber, whose research focuses on using infrasound, a low-frequency sound too deep for people to hear, and seismic data to study meteors and other fast-moving objects in the atmosphere. (Image credit: Logan Scamfer) Real-world tests So, in the big picture, having collaborative, multiple and independent ways to observe atmospheric entries is of benefit to planetary defense thinkers. "Planetary defense is not only about finding an object before it reaches Earth ," Silber said. "It is also about understanding what happens during atmospheric entry — that is, how the object f

item.title: Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide
item.description: Official poster for Tunde Kelani’s remastered political classic, “Agogo Èèwò.” If you watched Saworoide , get ready to return to Jogbo. Tunde Kelani ’s political drama Agogo Èèwò (2002), the follow-up to his acclaimed classic, is now available in a newly remastered presentation on TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ’s YouTube channel. Following the fall of military ruler Lagata in Saworoide, the people of Jogbo hope for a new era of peace and prosperity. But the corrupt chiefs have other plans. They install Adebosipo, played by the late veteran actor Dejumo Lewis , as the new king, believing that his background as a retired police officer will make him easy to control as they continue to exploit the kingdom’s treasury. Adebosipo, however, refuses to play along. Determined to protect the people of Jogbo, he demands accountability from the chiefs, setting off a fierce struggle over power, corruption and the future of the kingdom. The conflict reaches a defining moment during a public traditional oath-taking ceremony before the sacred Agogo Èèwò, or Gong of Taboo. Under the custom, anyone who has stolen from the land must confess before the gong sounds seven times, or face the consequences. Written by Professor Akinwunmi Isola and directed by Tunde Kelani, Agogo Èèwò remains a pointed examination of corruption, leadership and traditional systems of accountability. More than two decades after its original release, the film’s return in a remastered version gives audiences another opportunity to revisit the story and its enduring questions about those entrusted with power. The remastered Agogo Èèwò is now streaming on YouTube via TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ. Watch below The post Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Oleshky residents return to Ukraine
item.description: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-held territory following a rare local truce. They described years of isolation, food shortages and regular shelling, with some saying they were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive. Seized by Russian forces in the early days of the 2022 invasion, the city remains cut off by the Dnipro River on one side and Russian troops on the other.

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
item.description: null On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Ever since Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope to the red-tinted star and identified as a planet, Mars has captivated scientists' interests as to its nature. So it was of no surprise that as soon as we gained the ability to send missions into space, that the focus turned to the "fourth rock from the Sun." As it turned out, though, reaching Mars, let alone entering its orbit or landing on its surface,, was and continues to be difficult. Mars 1, despite its name, was actually the Soviet Union's fourth attempt at sending a probe to the planet. The first three ended in launch failures. Similar problems faced the United States, as well, but it was NASA's Mariner IV mission that became the first to successfully fly by Mars two years later. Still, as humanity continues to push forward to the day people land on, explore and live on Mars, the 1962 Soviet mission stands as the first to get close to revealing the first details about the planet. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.description: Goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp helped Manchester City to escape from Bromley with three points after a thrilling encounter with London City Lionesses. It was a statement performance from the home team, despite the defeat delivering a blow to any title ambitions they may have been quietly holding on to before kick-off. The gap between the hosts and the champions is now six points, after Hemp restored City’s lead following Jana Fernández’s equaliser. But that London City had even played their way into conversations about this season’s title contenders in their second season has been impressive. Continue reading...

item.title: From Nigeria to Senegal: Ibquake Performs at Historic Dakar 2026 Opening Ceremony
item.description: Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Senegal came alive yesterday at the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with a vibrant celebration of culture, history and African creativity. Among the performers on stage was Nigeria’s very own Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , who represented the country with a spoken word performance. The ceremony took place at the Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, just outside Dakar, marking a major moment in sporting history as the first Olympic event to be hosted on African soil. More than 1,100 performers took part in the showcase, which featured music, dance, visual arts and spoken word. Senegalese music legends Baaba Maal and Kiné Lam , music group Daara J Family , Gambian kora musician Sona Jobarteh and social media personality Khaby Lame were among the other names featured. Ibquake on stage with dancers and the lit Olympic cauldron at the Dakar 2026 opening ceremony. Stepping onto the global stage in a structured white gown with a sculptural bodice and braided detailing, Ibquake performed against a backdrop of dancers in feathered and textured costumes. Her verses celebrated African identity, heritage and the possibilities ahead for the continent’s young people. Among the lines she delivered were: “We carry a flame for the African child to look beyond the horizon… We are both root and revolution.” Reflecting on the experience, Ibquake shared a personal message online about what being part of the historic occasion meant to her. She imagined her daughter one day asking when the Olympics first came to Africa, and how she would be able to tell her she was there. She wrote: “My daughter will one day ask me when the first Olympics games happened in Africa. And I’ll answer with speed and alacrity. She’ll ask me how I know… And I’ll say… Because mummy was a part of it.” Ibquake surrounded by dancers during the opening ceremony in Senegal. She went on to describe her life as a testament to God’s goodness and reaffirmed her commitment to telling African stories “Powerfully… Boldly,” adding that Africa will always be great in her eyes. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games run from October 31 to November 13, bringing together approximately 2,700 young athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees and the Youth Refugee Olympic Team. Competitions span 25 sports and 153 medal events, with activities taking place in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Read today! .
